title: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations
abstract:
Abstract
                  Electrocyclizations are a fundamental class of pericyclic transformations that can proceed through thermal or photochemical pathways. Although thermal electrocyclizations have been implicated in numerous biosynthetic pathways, there are few examples of enzyme-mediated processes, and the structural requirements for efficient catalysis are poorly understood. Here we develop an artificial photoenzyme for 6π-electrocyclizations (PhotoElectroCyclase PEC1.3) by introducing ten mutations into a recently reported [2 + 2]-cyclase. PEC1.3 processes diverse acrylanilide substrates with exceptional yields, regiocontrol and stereocontrol. A 1.3-Å crystal structure shows the substrate ideally positioned for energy transfer from a genetically programmed benzophenone triplet sensitizer. Interestingly, hydrogen-bonding interactions that were critical to [2 + 2] cyclase activity were abandoned during evolution of PEC1.3. Instead, the enzyme employs a network of hydrophobic interactions to constrain the substrate into a reactive geometry for selective antarafacial electrocyclization, allowing PEC1.3 to retain activity at cryogenic temperatures where appreciable molecular motions are frozen out. This example of controlled reaction outcomes without polar substrate–enzyme contacts points towards selective conversions of substrates lacking functional handles.

title: Photothermal-driven CO2 hydrogenation to methanol on an integrated Au–MoS2–TiO2 catalyst
abstract: Light-driven CO2 hydrogenation to methanol is constrained by insufficient broadband light utilization and inefficient CO2 activation. Herein, we achieve highly efficient photothermal hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol on an integrated Au–MoS2–TiO2 catalyst, in which MoS2 is anchored on TiO2 to form an intimate interface, and Au nanoparticles (NPs) are deposited on MoS2–TiO2. We demonstrate that the MoS2–TiO2 interface induces the formation of few-layered MoS2 and transfers electrons from TiO2 to MoS2. MoS2 serves as the primary active phase for CO2 hydrogenation, while Au NPs enhance photo-to-heat conversion via the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect, thereby collectively facilitating CO2 activation under mild reaction conditions. Under photothermal conditions at 120°C in a continuous-flow reactor, the catalyst achieves 13.4% CO2 conversion with 84.7% methanol selectivity, and maintains stable performance over 400 hours without observable deactivation, underscoring it among the most competitive photothermal catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol.

title: Room temperature giant in-plane anomalous Hall effect in TbMn6Sn6
abstract: The anomalous Hall effect is the transverse voltage response in the presence of out-of-plane magnetization or non-zero Berry curvature, which, traditionally, is modulated by an out-of-plane magnetic field. Here we demonstrate a giant in-plane anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by coplanar magnetic fields in the quantum magnet TbMn6Sn6 at room temperature. The very large Hall conductivity arises in response to an applied in-plane magnetic field and results from the tilting of the ferrimagnetic axis of the Mn and Tb moments to the out of plane direction. With the in-plane magnetic field aligning the ferrimagnetic axis, the Berry curvature induced giant anomalous Hall effect is observed. Further, we show that the in-plane field induced AHE is more pronounced below the temperature induced spin reorientation, showing a 2π periodicity in angular dependent measurements. Unlike the in-plane Hall effect previously observed primarily at low temperatures, the AHE we observe here represents the largest room-temperature response reported in a single material. Our results reveal strong coupling between an in-plane magnetic field and out-of-plane Berry curvature, enabling new opportunities to engineer spintronic and quantum device responses at practical operating temperatures.

title: Nucleophile–electrophile chemistry produces a stable interphase for long-Life anode-Less lithium metal batteries
abstract: Anode-less lithium (Li) metal batteries (ALLMBs) represent the optimal cell architecture for maximizing energy density, yet their practical viability is severely hindered by poor cycling life. This limitation stems from the unstable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI), which drives continuous parasitic reactions with Li metal and induces severe interfacial degradation. Here we report a nucleophile–electrophile bridging strategy to construct a robust, passivating SEI that enables long-term stable cycling of ALLMBs. By leveraging a nucleophilic substitution mechanism, electron-rich organic species derived from the solvent, acting as nucleophiles, are covalently bridged by electron-deficient, boron-centred electrophiles derived from the anion. This molecular-level integration overcomes the inherent fragility of the SEI organic phase, generating mechanically robust oligoborates that resist interfacial degradation, along with lithium fluoride (LiF) nanocrystals nucleated in-situ to facilitate rapid Li+ transport. The resulting oligoborate–LiF hybrid SEI enables highly reversible Li plating/stripping and remarkably extends the ALLMB cycling life by 12-fold, maintaining 80% capacity over 300 cycles. The superior cyclability is maintained even under stringent practical conditions (high cathode loading, lean electrolyte supply, and pouch-cell operation). This work establishes a fundamentally new paradigm in interphase engineering, paving the way for high-energy, reliable ALLMBs.

title: Nanocatalytic modulation of thrombin-ferroptosis axis for efficient intervention of ischemic stroke
abstract: Ischemic stroke represents a leading cause of global mortality. Current therapeutic strategies, including recombinant tissue plasminogen activator and mechanical thrombectomy, are constrained by suboptimal recanalization, high recurrence rates, and reperfusion injury. In this work, we initially identified elevated intrathrombotic thrombin as a critical mediator of fibrinolytic resistance and a driver of ferroptosis-related neuronal injury following stroke. To specifically target this thrombin dysregulation, we designed ultrasmall tungsten-based polyoxometalate (W-POM) nanodots capable of penetrating the blood-brain barrier. In addition to their specific reactive oxygen species-scavenging capability, W-POM nanodots primarily modulate thrombin activity and attenuate its pathological signaling. In both thrombin-induced and ischemia-reperfusion injury models, W-POM nanodots significantly improve neurological outcomes by directly suppressing thrombin activity and inhibiting thrombin-driven ferroptosis. Furthermore, W-POM nanodots remodel the thrombotic microenvironment and reduce neuroinflammation, thereby conferring robust neuroprotection. This study highlights the thrombin-ferroptosis pathway as a key mechanistic axis in stroke and introduces a nanotherapeutic platform for targeted thrombin modulation in ischemic stroke therapy.

title: Molecular regulation and recurrent evolution of fungal bet-hedging conidiation
abstract: Bet-hedging (BH) mitigates risk in fluctuating environments by promoting phenotypic diversity within a single genotype. Fungi exhibit remarkable phenotypic plasticity, such as conidiation polymorphism. Here, we show that entomopathogenic Metarhizium

title: Designing solar panels for realistic end-of-life scenarios
abstract: The rapid growth of photovoltaics is generating vast waste streams, a portion of which flows to regions where recycling is unregulated. Solar panel design criteria do not account for these end-of-life realities, creating global asymmetry in environmental burdens. This Comment proposes research directions beyond material substitution to address these design gaps.

title: Ultralow-volume shallow microwell-based collection and processing for scalable spatial proteome mapping of tissues
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multi-ome mapping technologies for precise comprehensive characterization of tissues at high spatial resolutions are crucial for providing insights into tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment within spatial context. However, proteome mapping technologies lag far behind other transcriptome (genome) mapping technologies. Here we report an Ultralow-volume, Shallow, Microwell plate-based voxel Collection and Processing coupled with mass spectrometry (MS) method, termed USMCP-MS, for robust scalable proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions. This method was built upon the design of an ultralow-volume, shallow 96-well plate for robust rapid collection and processing of single voxels. Using a commonly accessible MS platform, USMCP-MS enables reproducible label-free quantification of ~1,700 and ~2,500 protein groups from single voxels of fresh frozen mouse brain tissue at 20 µm × 20 µm × 10 µm ( ~ 1 cell region) and 50 µm × 50 µm × 10 µm ( ~ 6 cell region), respectively. More importantly, USMCP-MS can be broadly applied to different types of tissues (fresh frozen, OCT-embedded, and FFPE) for 2D proteome mapping of region areas of interest at 50–100 µm spatial resolutions, revealing spatially resolved protein signatures and region-specific signaling pathways. With its further improvement, USMCP-MS may pave the way for routine, robust, scalable proteome mapping of tissues at single-cell spatial resolution.

title: Nanotechnology Meets Brain Diseases: Emerging Therapeutic Strategies for Drug Delivery
abstract: Abstract Brain diseases, encompassing neurodegenerative disorders, cerebrovascular diseases, and brain tumors, impose a profound global health burden. Conventional therapeutic strategies often fail due to the formidable blood–brain barrier (BBB) and complex pathological microenvironment of the central nervous system (CNS). The rapid evolution of nanotechnology offers unprecedented opportunities to overcome these delivery hurdles. This review comprehensively summarizes recent developments in engineered nanoplatforms for the diagnosis and targeted therapy of brain diseases. It first outlines the pathological characteristics and nanoprobe-enhanced diagnostic methods for various brain disorders, followed by a critical evaluation of five major classes of nanocarriers for CNS drug delivery: lipid-based, polymeric, inorganic, bio-derived, and hybrid nanocarriers. This evaluation highlights their structural attributes and delivery efficiencies. The discussion then examines advanced strategies to improve delivery precision, including multilevel targeting (e.g., BBB penetration and specific cell targeting), stimuli-responsive theranostics, and functional surface modifications. Linking these nanotechnological innovations to specific neurological diseases highlights their clinical potential. Finally, the review addresses current translational challenges, including biosafety, scalable manufacturing, and interindividual variability, and offers a forward-looking perspective on the rational design of next-generation precision neuro-nanomedicines.

title: Structural Insights into Erm-Mediated rRNA Methylation Underlying Antibiotic Resistance
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract SAM-dependent Erm enzymes confer resistance to clinically important MLSB antibiotics (macrolides–lincosamides–streptogramin B) by methylation of the rRNA (rRNA) target. However, the molecular basis of the Erm–rRNA interaction remains poorly understood, hindering the development of effective Erm inhibitors to preserve antibiotic efficacy. Here, we integrate NMR and computational data to investigate the interaction between ErmB, prevalent in pathogenic Gram-positive bacteria, and a minimal RNA substrate mimicking the rRNA target. We demonstrate that Erm–RNA complex formation is critically dependent on the SAM cofactor, which shapes the conformational space of the entire catalytic domain, priming ErmB for specific recognition of its RNA substrate. Using NMR-guided docking, we derive experimentally validated structural models of the ErmB–RNA complex that reveal a vast and dynamic binding interface comprising ErmB’s N- and C-terminal domains, as well as the cationic interdomain cleft. These insights into the Erm enzyme function provide a foundation for the rational design of potent and selective drugs to combat pathogenic bacteria.

title: A Zwitterionic Polymeric Quaternary Ammonium Microparticle (Z-pQAM) as a Candidate Wound Dressing with Simultaneous Procoagulant, Antimicrobial, and Wound-Healing Activities
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Wound infection, inadequate local hemostasis, and delayed healing remain major complications following surgery and in chronic wounds. Effective wound management requires materials that simultaneously prevent infection, support hemostasis, promote tissue repair, and maintain biocompatibility. Here, we synthesized a zwitterionic polymeric quaternary ammonium microparticle (Z-pQAM) and evaluated its biocompatibility, in vitro antimicrobial and procoagulant activity, and wound-healing effects. FTIR confirmed stepwise synthesis and quaternization, and zeta potential analysis showed that Z-pQAM retains a net-negative bulk surface charge across physiological pH. In vitro degradation studies in PBS showed that Z-pQAM retained >99% of its dry mass after three weeks, indicating slow, physiologically appropriate hydrolytic degradation. Functional assays are in line with the hypothesis that its procoagulant and antibacterial activity arise from locally accessible quaternary ammonium (QA+) microdomains rather than overall surface positivity. Z-pQAM achieved >7-log10 reduction against S. aureus and E. coli, and >5-log10 reduction against MRSA at 200 mg/mL, with Live/Dead staining confirming bactericidal membrane disruption, while maintaining <0.5% hemolysis and 100% cell viability across the tested concentration range. In recalcified whole blood, Z-pQAM achieved a blood clotting index of 36.5%, comparable to a benchmark FDA-cleared hemostatic powder. In an uninfected murine full-thickness excisional wound model, topical Z-pQAM accelerated closure at day 8 without altering epidermal thickness, reduced CD45+ inflammatory infiltration by >50% at day 3, and enhanced collagen deposition by day 12. Collectively, these findings position Z-pQAM as a promising candidate for a multifunctional topical wound dressing, combining antibacterial and procoagulant activity with biocompatibility and support for wound repair.

title: GO Coating-Assisted Deformation and Failure Regulation of Glass Fibers under High-Speed Impact
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Continuous glass fiber (GF) reinforced polymers (GFRPs) are widely used in high-performance applications due to their excellent mechanical properties. A new coating strategy involving coating graphene oxide (GO) on the fibers has been shown to effectively enhance the mechanical properties and durability of their 3D printed composites. However, their performance under high-speed impact loading deserves attention. In this study, the reinforcement mechanism of GO coatings on GF substrates under high-speed bending conditions is investigated using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Both single-layer and bilayer GO coatings were evaluated to understand their effects on impact-induced deformation behavior and energy dissipation capacity. The results demonstrate that GO coatings significantly enhance the resistance to impact-induced deformation, resulting in increases in the perforation threshold velocity of 46.9 and 71.9% for single-layer and bilayer coatings, respectively. The presence of GO coatings introduces distinct deformation and failure behaviors, thereby enhancing energy absorption and improving resistance to impact-induced perforation. These findings offer valuable insights into optimizing GO-coated GFs for applications requiring enhanced impact resistance, such as aerospace, automotive safety, and protective components.

title: Green-Solvent-Processed Janus Membranes for Subambient Radiative Cooling and Unidirectional Sweat Transport
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Extreme heat events are escalating globally, driving an urgent need for personal thermal-wet management materials. However, existing radiative cooling textiles face a persistent trilemma, including toxic organic solvents, efficient sweat dissipation with sacrificed cooling, and end-of-life recyclability. Here, we break this trade-off by a green-solvent-processed moisture-thermal management membrane (G-MTMM) via sequential electrospinning. This membrane consists of hydrophobic polyvinyl butyral skin layer and hydrophilic alcohol-soluble nylon/Al2O3 environmental layer, creating an asymmetric wettability and pore-size gradient. This design achieves solar reflectance of 95.46% and atmospheric-window emissivity of 90.80%, driven by multiscale Mie scattering from the hierarchical network and γ-Al2O3 nanoparticles, complemented by complementary molecular vibrations of polymers and Al–O lattice phonons. Under 100 mW cm–2 simulated sunlight, G-MTMM reduces the temperature of a simulated skin by 14.9 °C compared with cotton, and outdoor tests demonstrate a subambient cooling of –3.17 °C under peak solar irradiance. The Laplace pressure difference arising from the wettability and pore-size contrast enables unidirectional liquid sweat transport from the hydrophobic skin side to the hydrophilic environment side with a one-way transport index of 734.5% and anti-gravity pumping capability. G-MTMM also exhibits excellent flexibility, mechanical durability, washability, and closed-loop recyclability, offering a novel paradigm for sustainable personal thermal-wet comfort.

title: Garnet Nanofiber Scaffolds and Sulfonated Graphene Enable Stable Li+ Transport in Polymer Electrolytes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The practical application of solid polymer electrolytes remains limited by sluggish Li+ transport and insufficient interfacial stability. Herein, a PVDF-HFP-based composite solid polymer electrolyte was developed by incorporating Al-doped garnet-type LLZO nanofibers (LLZAO) and sulfonated graphene (SG) as functional components into the PVDF-HFP matrix. This design creates a continuous ceramic transport scaffold and a polar interfacial network. LLZAO provides mechanical reinforcement and long-range Li+ transport pathways, whereas the sulfonic acid sites of SG promote lithium salt dissociation and regulate local Li+ coordination and anion distribution. Synchrotron X-ray tomography, synchrotron radiation Fourier transform infrared (SR-FTIR), in situ small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy/X-ray absorption near-edge structure (sXAS/XANES), and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) further reveal that the three-dimensionally interconnected LLZAO fiber scaffold establishes a continuous Li+ transport network. Meanwhile, the polar sites of SG enhance lithium salt dissociation and regulate interfacial coordination. Together, these components stabilize the nanoscale multiphase structure during cycling. The resulting electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.6 × 10–4 S cm–1 at 60 °C. This work provides a new strategy for the synergistic construction of continuous ion-transport pathways and stable coordination interfaces in composite polymer electrolytes.

title: Fluorination‑driven σ‑bonding design enables practical aqueous zinc-vanadium‑oxide batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Vanadium-based positive electrodes for aqueous batteries offer high-capacity, low-cost energy storage but are limited by vanadium dissolution and sluggish kinetics. Amorphization alleviates kinetic limitations by creating open ion-transport pathways, yet vanadium dissolution remains unresolved. Here, we propose a coordination-engineering strategy that stabilizes amorphous vanadium oxides via fluorine incorporation, thereby suppressing vanadium dissolution without compromising fast ion-transport kinetics. Replacing O2- with highly electronegative F- converts labile σ + π V-O coordination into robust σ-dominated V-F coordination. The resulting V-F bonding weakens interactions with H2O and suppresses water-induced degradation, whereas the comparable ionic radii of F- and O2- allow substitution without perturbing amorphous framework, preserving fast ion transport. Consequently, aqueous zinc-ion batteries assembled with the fluorinated amorphous vanadium oxide positive electrode exhibit fast kinetics and long-term cycling stability, delivering a high specific capacity of 155.6 mAh g−1 at 200 A g−1, stable cycling for up to 70,000 cycles at 100 A g−1, and durable operation at 0.1 A g−1 (20 mg cm−2) for over six months. This work shows that fluorine-induced reconstruction of the local coordination environment can resolve the stability-kinetics trade-off in amorphous electrodes, providing a microscopic-to-macroscopic design principle for aqueous batteries.

title: Mesophase-induced vitrification in coordination polymers via aliphatic chain dynamics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hybrid glasses of coordination polymers promise a fusion of processability and structural functionality, yet their formation is limited by poor thermal stability and high melting points. Here, we show mesophase-induced vitrification in a series of magnesium-based coordination polymers with aliphatic dicarboxylate linkers of varying chain length. Upon thermal desolvation, these frameworks transition into a mesomorphic state that retains the long-range order of the parent framework while disordering the organic substructure. This intermediate state enables a direct glass transition without melting. In contrast, only the longest-chain analogue melts, and its melt-quenched glass has lower stiffness owing to partial dissociation of the metal–organic backbone, indicating that mechanical properties are governed by the integrity of the coordination network. Spectroscopic and structural analyses show that vitrification proceeds through mobilisation of the aliphatic linker within an intact coordination network, paralleling semicrystalline polymers. These findings establish a design strategy for vitrifiable coordination networks that integrates principles from polymer dynamics and mesomorphism.

title: Intramolecular electrophilic aminations of indoles enable divergent bond migrations to access piperidinoindolines and δ-carbolines
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: In contrast to well-established C–C migration rearrangements of spiro[indole-3,3’-pyrrolidine] systems, analogous transformations involving isomeric spiro[indole-3,2’-pyrrolidine] frameworks remain unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that unprotected spiro[indole-3,2’-pyrrolidine] intermediates can be generated via acid-catalyzed deprotection of indoles equipped with C3-tethered activated hydroxylamine units. Subsequent migration of the N-center from the C3 to the C2 position of the indolenine is followed by aerobic oxidation or trapping with electrophiles to yield piperidinoindolines. Notably, spiro[indole-3,2’-pyrrolidine] systems with an aryl substituent at C3’ undergo C–C migration in preference to C–N migration, leading to δ-carbolines. Related reactions employing indoles with C2-tethered aminating units are also presented. These strategies offer efficient and concise routes to synthetically challenging piperidinoindoline and δ-carboline scaffolds. The mechanisms of these new processes have been investigated experimentally and via density functional theory calculations. Furthermore, preliminary biological evaluation has revealed potent antitumor activity in selected derivatives.

title: LitMOF: An LLM Multi-Agent for Literature-Validated Metal-Organic Frameworks Database Correction and Expansion
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors propagate through high-throughput screening and machine-learning workflows, limiting the reliability of data-driven materials discovery. Repairing them is difficult because the necessary evidence is scattered across crystallographic files, synthesis descriptions, and the primary literature. Here we present LitMOF, a multi-agent framework driven by large language models that reads the original publication for each structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry to repair errors. Applying LitMOF to the metal–organic framework subset of the Cambridge Structural Database, we assembled LitMOF-DB, a curated set of 189,567 computation-ready structures that includes 9,277 repaired entries, or 69.1% of the not-computation-ready structures in the latest CoRE MOF database. The system also recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks missing from existing resources. Using direct air capture screening as a case study, we show that structural errors distort predicted adsorption energies and CO2/H2O selectivity, which misranks materials, produces false positives, and omits high-performing candidates. This work offers a route toward self-correcting scientific databases and toward database curation driven by large language models.

title: 3D-printed Eutectic high-entropy alloys with dynamic protection for tribological damage resistance
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Maintaining the structural integrity of metallic materials under extreme localized shear poses a significant challenge for engineering reliability in the aerospace, automotive, and energy sectors, as such loading readily triggers catastrophic strain localization and surface delamination. Here, we report a nanoarchitecture-driven dynamic protection strategy to overcome this challenge. We engineer an FCC-dominant nanolamellar (FCC-NL) architecture in an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) by combining additive manufacturing (AM) with metastability engineering. Rather than undergoing the structural degradation observed in conventional EHEAs, this AM-enabled FCC-NL architecture orchestrates a robust hierarchical protective structure under severe sliding. It concurrently drives the bottom-up mechanochemical assembly of a damage-tolerant amorphous-nanocrystalline γ-Fe2O3 tribolayer and the top-down mechanical assembly of a strain-isolating nacre-like subsurface. This synergy yields a wear rate of 5.8 × 10−6 mm3 N−1 m−1, achieving an order-of-magnitude enhancement in surface damage resistance that surpasses currently reported values for bulk HEAs. This dynamic protection concept provides a design framework for developing highly surface-damage-tolerant alloys, essential to the reliability of critical engineering systems.

title: Non Hermitian synthetic phase shifter with topologically protected phase control via tunable losses
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Phase shifters are fundamental reconfigurable components in photonic circuits. In conjunction with passive elements, they control light flow and serve as foundational building blocks for diverse applications, including communication, sensing, analog signal processing, and quantum control. Conventional phase shifters achieve phase control by modulating the refractive index through various physical mechanisms such as thermo-optic or electro-optic effects. However, despite expectations that such index–based approaches would integrate seamlessly, they, in practice, restrict circuit size, bandwidth, and scalability and thus become bottlenecks to large–scale photonic integration. Here, we introduce an alternative phase–control approach based on optical loss modulation. We demonstrate a synthetic phase shifter that uses two independently controlled loss–modulation stages combined with multipath interference to achieve full–cycle phase tunability while maintaining constant amplitude. We develop a theoretical framework based on conserved topological charges to show how synthetic phase control can be achieved via non-Hermitian effects, enabling robust, topologically protected phase control. By shifting the paradigm from index control to loss modulation, the proposed synthetic phase shifter could pave the way for scalable integrated photonic systems that support applications from communications and sensing to photonic classical and quantum information processing.

title: Quasi-degenerate cation occupation enables oxygen-vacancy defect healing in nonlinear optical crystals
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chemical substitution is an effective strategy to enhance the desired performances of materials based on known structural prototypes. However, it almost invariably introduces intrinsic defects, such as vacancies and twinning defects, which couple with dopants and obscure or degrade the intrinsic properties. Therefore, chemical substitution that enables atomically precise engineering of materials without generating defect structures remains challenging. Here, we propose a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to overcome this detrimental coupling and successfully apply it to the langasite-family nonlinear optical (NLO) crystal, La3TiGa5O14 (LGTi). Therein, the cross-site occupation of Ti and Ti3+/Ti4+ redox flexibility improves the kinetic accessibility of oxygen-vacancy (VO) defects associated with cation disorder, enabling their removal during oxidative annealing. The oxidized LGTi single crystal has a VO-related defect concentration below the electron paramagnetic resonance detection limit, with a laser damage threshold of 2.53 GW/cm2 and a large NLO coefficient of 3.51 pm/V, both exceeding the previously reported values for bulk langasite-family crystals. Overall, this work provides a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to mitigate substitution-induced defects in structurally complex crystalline systems and has great prospects in enhancing material performance.

title: Photocatalytic control of diamond color center charge states via laser-induced surface oxidation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Color center spins in diamond nanostructures are a key resource for emerging quantum technologies. Their innate surface proximity makes precise control of diamond surface chemistry essential for optimizing their functionality and charge states. However, conventional surface functionalization methods provide limited control over the resulting surface termination and color-center charge state. Here, we demonstrate nonvolatile tuning of diamond’s surface termination through laser-induced oxidation of H-terminated diamond nanopillars. By tracking negatively charged silicon-vacancy (SiV−) photoluminescence as a charge-state proxy, we elucidate the carrier-assisted nature of this photocatalytic process through systematic photon-flux and photon-energy analyses, identifying defect charge cycling as a source of photogenerated carriers that drive the interfacial redox chemistry responsible for surface oxidation. Our results suggest that this approach may be applicable to other color centers and host materials for charge-state control and surface engineering in solid-state quantum devices.

title: Biomass-based platform for pesticide management balancing field efficacy with postharvest residue via dynamic adhesion switch
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recent nanopesticide formulations with strong adhesion enhance field efficacy by improving droplet retention on plant surfaces; however, their prolonged retention may increase postharvest residue risks, making it challenging to balance field performance with postharvest safety. Here we show a thermoresponsive adhesion switch inspired by biological adhesion mechanisms, employing lignin as a biomass-based platform to create a Pickering emulsion system (LgN-PE@EB) loaded with emamectin benzoate (EB). The system regulates its interfacial behavior with leaf surfaces through temperature-dependent phase transitions, achieving ~136% higher droplet retention than EB-EC under cultivation conditions and 114-275% increase in wash-off efficiency during postharvest cold-water washing. Additionally, lignin-derived UV shielding improves pesticide stability, while insecticidal activity (LC50) and biological safety (by crop fresh weight) increase by 64.9% and 61.1-165.9%, respectively. Overall, LgN-PE@EB provides a solution to address the spatiotemporal requirements of cultivation and postharvest, enhancing harvest flexibility and export safety for raw and high-value crops.

title: Marine volatile organic compounds air-sea exchange dynamics across a summer-to-autumn ecosystem transition
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Marine ecosystems influence atmospheric chemistry and climate by exchanging volatile organic compounds (VOCs) with the atmosphere, yet the chemical diversity and the environmental controls of the exchanged compounds remain poorly constrained. This gap persists because most marine observations are targeted, short-term, and narrow-suite measurements that seldom deliver chemically broad, continuous fluxes. Here we show that marine VOC exchange is chemically diverse and changes in magnitude and composition on event‑to‑season timescales. Using continuous flux measurements of 73 m/z features in the Baltic Sea, we observe a pronounced reorganization of net exchange: early organosulfur emissions diminish as cyanobacterial biomass declines (indicating water-side source limitation), while oxygenated and nitrogen-containing VOCs exhibit mixed behaviors ranging from deposition to episodic emissions (often dominated by wind-driven gas transfer kinetics). Together, these results demonstrate that chemically diverse marine VOC exchange is closely coupled to wind-induced mixing, water‑column structure, and phytoplankton community succession, highlighting the need to resolve these dynamic ecosystem states to predict future atmospheric composition.

title: A conceptual analysis of One Health and Person-Centred Practice
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Climate change, emerging infectious diseases and widening inequalities show that the health of people, animals and ecosystems cannot be separated. However, the ideas we use to understand this interdependence and those we use to organise and practise care have largely developed apart. Here we bring together One Health, linking human, animal and environmental health, and person-centred practice, focused on dignity, relationships and meaningful care. We show where they meet, where they clash and what each offers the other, arguing that care without responsibility for animals and ecosystems is incomplete, as is One Health without attention to lived experience.

title: Nationwide high-resolution assessment reveals the underestimated carbon sink of Chinese parks
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Against the backdrop of global efforts to address climate change and promote carbon neutrality, parks, as Nature-based solutions, are often underestimated in their collective carbon sequestration function. Here we establish a high-resolution (30 -meter) carbon accounting framework for 8,137 parks across mainland China from 2010 to 2020, incorporating previously overlooked small parks. We show that parks constitute a substantial carbon sink. The total carbon sequestration based on Net Primary Productivity of parks nationwide reaches 52.7 million tonnes of carbon in 2020. Within the 5,425 urban parks, large parks exceeding 100 hectares (hm²) contribute over 90% of the total urban park sequestration, whereas parks of 10–50 hm2 drive the 2010–2020 shift from carbon sources to sinks. Medium and small sized parks show greater synergy between carbon sequestration and recreation services, informing locally tailored planning.

title: Longitudinal changes in mis-splicing in a cohort of female twins are widespread and highlight mechanisms of ageing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ageing is characterised by widespread cellular and molecular dysregulation including broad changes to gene expression. To study the impact of ageing on alternative splicing we profiled whole-blood RNA-seq data from 318 female twins (median age 61) at three time points over 6-8 years. We observe longitudinal changes across multiple classes of alternative splicing. Notably, intron retention, a marker of mis-splicing, shows a striking increase over time (P = 5.2 × 10−5). Twin modelling demonstrates that intron retention within an individual is heritable, with heritability increasing from 0.44 to 0.55 over time. Intron retention levels inversely associate with expression of RNA-binding proteins including SRSF4, ELAVL1, and AGO1, and show time-varying positive associations with diabetes status and markers of kidney disease, suggesting a link to chronic disease. Together, these findings suggest that mis-splicing is a heritable feature of human ageing which increases in prevalence over time and is associated with age-related disease.

title: Beyond facility-level metrics: A whole-system energy–water nexus analysis of data centre integration in Great Britain’s net-zero transition
abstract: The rapid proliferation of hyperscale data centres (DCs) presents compounded challenges to Great Britain (GB)’s net-zero energy transition, superimposing large, continuously growing electricity loads on an energy system simultaneously aiming to be net-zero by 2050. However, existing assessments of DC sustainability rely largely on facility-level metrics such as Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE), which provide limited insight into indirect water use and the cross-sector effects of DC integration on power-system infrastructure and decarbonisation pathways. Here, we develop a spatially explicit whole-system energy–water nexus optimisation model for 13 GB regions, representing air-cooled, water-cooled, and direct-to-chip (D2C) cooling architectures. The model uses 24-hour resolution within weighted representative days and a rolling-horizon solution approach with a one-period look-ahead, with weather-dependent PUE and WUE derived from regional typical-meteorological-year data. Under the modelled scenarios, 21.7 GW of installed DC IT capacity adds 124–133 TWh/yr of electricity demand to the GB energy system by 2050, and water-cooled configurations consume 297 × 10 9 litres/yr of direct, on-site cooling water, compared with 31 × 10 9 litres/yr for air cooling. DC integration also increases indirect water consumption by 229 -- 255 × 10 9 litres/yr through the additional generation required, almost entirely from nuclear generation. Relative to water cooling, D2C cooling reduces total system water consumption by 322 × 10 9 litres/yr, almost entirely through the elimination of direct water use, while differences between the three configurations in electricity generation ( 6 TWh/yr between D2C and water cooling), indirect water and heat supply lie within the numerical variability of the optimisation. Under hypothetical water-availability constraints, the air-cooled configuration remains feasible down to 70% of its unconstrained regional water consumption, at which system cost rises by 4.7% (from £593 to £621 billion), solar capacity increases by 25 GW, nuclear capacity falls by 11 GW, and DC capacity relocates from NT and SW towards SO, WN, NO and SC. The water-cooled configuration remains feasible only down to 95% availability, because its direct cooling water cannot be reduced without changing the installed DC capacity. In an exploratory analysis, integrating DC waste heat with Direct Air Capture (DAC) installs 59 MtCO 2 /yr of fully utilised DAC capacity by 2050, using 87% of the available waste heat and adding 11 TWh/yr of electricity demand. Relative to the D2C, net CO 2 emissions decrease from − 9 to − 68 MtCO 2 /yr, system cost (excluding the reserve-margin penalty) rises by £4–5 billion, while changes in generation and installed capacity remain within the variability between independent solutions, reflecting that DAC deployment is driven by the carbon price applied to net emissions rather than by the net-zero constraint, which is already met without DAC. These results indicate that the system-level consequences of DC deployment can differ from those inferred from facility-level PUE and WUE metrics alone, highlighting the importance of jointly considering electricity, water, cooling, heating, and negative-emissions interactions in planning future DC infrastructure.

title: Spatiotemporal brain dynamics of limb ownership perception
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We experience our limbs as our own, but how does the brain generate this fundamental sense of body ownership? Previous studies have relied mainly on fMRI or lesion mapping, providing a static view of the neural mechanisms underlying body ownership. Using magnetoencephalography, robotically controlled visuotactile stimulation, and multivariate analysis across the rubber hand illusion, a real hand condition, and multiple control conditions, we identified source vector dissimilarity patterns reflecting ownership of the left arm. Three phases of ownership-specific activity patterns emerged: (i) anticipatory patterns in medial frontal cortex, right posterior parietal cortex, and right posterior cerebellum before tactile stimulation; (ii) multisensory integration patterns in right dorsal and ventral premotor cortex, right posterior parietal cortex, and anterior cerebellum at 116–156 ms poststimulus; and (iii) later bilateral insular and left hemisphere patterns at 184–232 ms. These findings provide a whole-brain, time-resolved map of activity patterns underlying body ownership, revealing its dynamic neural construction.

title: A scalable pipeline for patient-matched pediatric solid tumor models and cell lines
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Most pediatric solid tumor cell lines were established decades ago, and patient-matched organoids and xenografts are rarely available, limiting their translational utility. We present an approach to generate triads of patient-matched xenografts, three-dimensional organoids, and two-dimensional primary cultures from pediatric tumors, including rhabdomyosarcoma, osteosarcoma, neuroblastoma, Ewing sarcoma, Wilms tumor, and retinoblastoma. We have generated organoids from 135 pediatric tumors, alongside 82 patient-matched two-dimensional primary cultures and 20 new cell lines. When orthotopically implanted into immunocompromised mice, these models preserved the molecular and cellular features of the original patient tumor. We completed 365 single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing experiments encompassing over 2.2 million cells to evaluate cellular heterogeneity across triads. All samples are renewable, and over 3000 vials have been cryopreserved for unrestricted distribution through the Childhood Solid Tumor Network. In this work, we present a comprehensive methodological toolbox for generating patient-matched triads for advancing preclinical pediatric cancer research.

title: Prioritizing the next decade of research in bat infectious disease (batID)
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bats are widely studied as asymptomatic hosts of viruses that cause high case fatality rates in humans. Though prior research into bat infections has been traditionally virus-focused, there is growing interest to more holistically understand bat-microbe relationships. In July 2025 the fourth International Symposium on the Infectious Diseases of Bats (‘BatID 2025’) convened, synthesizing the current state of bat-microbe research from within-host to population-level processes. Here, we outline five questions that emerged from this meeting as priority future directions. We share this review with the aim of stimulating future research, emphasizing the need for data sharing and interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: Water-energy-carbon nexus footprint of seawater desalination and transfer for industrial development: a hybrid life cycle -node-flow framework
abstract: Seawater desalination is becoming increasingly important in arid, industrializing regions, but planning assessments often consider the embodied energy of supply chains and the operational energy of water transfer separately. This study presents a hybrid life cycle and node-flow framework that combines embodied energy and carbon emissions with a spatially explicit model of pumping energy based on elevation gain and hydraulic head losses. The framework is applied to Iran's Persian Gulf Seawater Desalination and Transfer (SDT) project, which supplies 138.76 million m 3 of water annually. Two strategies are compared: Water Transfer (WT), which pumps water inland while transporting products to the coast, and Industrial Transfer (IT), which relocates industries to the coast and transports raw materials from inland areas. Rail and truck freight represent the best- and worst-case transport scenarios, respectively. Pumping-energy intensity ranges from 333.2 to 21,462.4 MWh per million m 3 , depending mainly on transfer distance and elevation. Although industrial relocation reduces long-distance pumping-energy by 99.4%, transporting raw materials offsets much of this saving. Under the grid-average electricity scenario, rail transport results in nearly unchanged total energy use (+0.9%) but reduces carbon emissions by 22.7%. With truck transport, energy use and carbon emissions increase by 121.9% and 53.8%, respectively. Under low-carbon electricity, relocation increases carbon emissions with both transport modes. Benefits also vary by industry: relocation reduces energy use at the steel site under both modes and at the pelletizing site by rail, but not at the copper sites, where raw-material requirements are substantially greater than product output. The water footprint changes only slightly (−4.4%). This framework supports integrated assessments of energy and carbon trade-offs in desalination-dependent industrial systems.

title: Data-driven distributionally robust planning of coastal distribution networks and PV-storage-EV stations for low-carbon energy transition
abstract: Coastal distribution networks (DNs) are becoming key infrastructure for the low-carbon energy transition as electric vehicle (EV) charging, photovoltaic (PV) generation, energy storage, and marine renewable procurement are increasingly coupled at the planning stage. Existing planning models, however, usually treat network expansion, PV-storage-EV station (PSES) deployment, low-carbon operation, and coastal asset degradation separately. This paper proposes a data-driven distributionally robust planning framework for coastal DNs and PSESs. The framework jointly optimizes radial network topology and PSES siting while incorporating salt-spray degradation costs, carbon-emission-flow (CEF)-based nodal carbon accounting, and tidal-generation-driven procurement costs. To represent heterogeneous uncertainty, the model combines continuous box uncertainty for load and PV availability with probability ambiguity over EV-charging scenarios generated from historical charging profiles. The resulting two-stage distributionally robust optimization problem is reformulated through exact relaxation of ESS mode binaries and KKT-based decomposition, and is solved by an inexact column-and-constraint generation (i-C&CG) algorithm. Case studies on a realistic 47-node coastal feeder show that salt-spray exposure can alter the selected topology and PSES siting, while the proposed planning scheme improves voltage quality, reduces annualized total cost, and reveals the cost--carbon trade-off of tidal procurement. The tailored i-C&CG algorithm obtains the same optimal design as conventional C&CG with about an order-of-magnitude reduction in solution time.

title: Covalent Interfacial Engineering for Suppressing Defect and Phonon-Mediated Losses in Perovskite Quantum Dots/Polymer Composites
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Addressing the synergistic nonradiative losses in CsPbBr3 perovskite quantum dots (PQDs)/polymer composites arising from interfacial defects and lattice softness is crucial for enhancing the photoluminescence performance. This study proposes a molecular interface engineering strategy employing the crosslinkable ligand 2-carboxyethyl acrylate (CEA). By constructing coordination-covalent bonds and covalent interfaces between CEA-modified CsPbBr3 PQDs and a polymer matrix formed via the copolymerization of CEA and pentaerythritol triacrylate monomer, the resulting composites achieve a photoluminescence quantum yield of 78% along with enhanced water and thermal stability, retaining approximately 83% of their initial emission intensity after 15 days of water immersion and 41% emission intensity at 393 K after continuous heating. Femtosecond transient absorption and variable-temperature photoluminescence spectra reveal that the covalent interfaces not only passivate surface defects and suppress nonradiative recombination but also effectively reduce exciton-phonon coupling and multi-phonon relaxation processes by enhancing lattice rigidity and increasing optical phonon energy.

title: Immunoglobulin A promotes stable colonization of Bifidobacterium to protect against allergic inflammation under fiber deprivation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Modern dietary patterns, particularly those low in fermentable fiber, are associated with intestinal dysbiosis and increased susceptibility to allergic disease, yet individuals exposed to similar diets often display markedly different outcomes. This variability suggests that protective commensal microbes may persist in some hosts, but the mechanisms that maintain these bacteria and enable their immunoregulatory effects remain unclear. Here, we show that Bifidobacterium induces self-recognizing, T cell–dependent immunoglobulin A (IgA) that enhances its mucosal adhesion and persistence under fiber-deprived conditions. Loss of this IgA response reduces Bifidobacterium colonization and increases allergic inflammation. We further demonstrate that Bifidobacterium-derived metabolites, including genistein and indole-3-lactic acid (ILA), suppress mast cell (MC) activation and T helper 2 (Th2) responses through distinct mechanisms, attenuating allergic inflammation and systemic anaphylaxis in vivo. Together, these findings reveal a self-reinforcing host–microbial mutualism in which adaptive IgA preserves, rather than eliminates, beneficial commensals to maintain immune homeostasis.

title: ALKR1275Q expands Schwann cell precursor-like cells during sympathoadrenal commitment, creating a permissive state for neuroblastoma initiation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) arises from neural crest-derived cells of the sympathoadrenal lineage, yet how predisposing genetic lesions influence early human development remains poorly understood. Here, we use patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models carrying the familial ALK R1275Q mutation to investigate its role during sympathoadrenal differentiation. We show that ALK R1275Q delays lineage maturation and sustains a proliferative progenitor state characterized by elevated ALK signaling and expansion of a Schwann cell precursor (SCP)-like population. This SCP-like state persists during differentiation and is reduced by ALK inhibition or CRISPR-based mutation correction. Although ALK R1275Q alone is insufficient to drive tumor formation in vivo, it enhances susceptibility to oncogenic transformation in cooperation with MYCN. Together, these findings support a model in which ALK R1275Q reshapes developmental trajectories by maintaining a proliferative SCP-like progenitor state, thereby creating a permissive cellular context for NB initiation.

title: CARM1-mediated methylation controls interactions of ALIX with key partners important for cytokinesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: CARM1 is an arginine methyltransferase with a well-established role in regulating gene expression, but its cytoplasmic functions remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we identified ALIX, a cytoplasmic protein acting with the ESCRT-III machinery in numerous membrane remodeling events, as a partner and substrate of CARM1. We demonstrate that CARM1 methylates arginine residues within the proline-rich motif of ALIX. At the molecular level, ALIX methylation impairs SH3-dependent association with CD2AP, CIN85, and endophilin-A2 that are required for cytokinesis. Using a mutant of ALIX that is unable to bind these proteins, we further show that these interactions are essential for ALIX functions during cytokinesis. Mechanistically, ALIX methylation controls the levels of CD2AP at the cytokinetic midbody, which are known to be critical for successful cytokinesis. Altogether, this work highlights the significance of arginine methylation as a regulatory post-translational modification important for the final step of cell division, by modulating interactions between proline-rich domains and their SH3-containing partners.

title: Harnessing plant cells as oral drug delivery capsules for synergistic therapy of ulcerative colitis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cell-derived carriers are important excipients in drug delivery systems; however, most studies have focused on mammalian cells. Plant cells, by comparison, offer intrinsic therapeutic potential and feature a bilayer structure composed of cell wall and cell membrane. Here, we utilize the carrot plant cells as oral colon-targeting drug delivery vehicles leveraging their intrinsic therapeutic properties and the outer layer of cell wall. Utilizing ulcerative colitis and glucocorticoid budesonide as a disease and drug model, the drug loading strategy, colon microenvironment sensitivity, colon-specific drug release and anti-inflammation efficacies of the plant cell-based delivery system are evaluated. In particular, the budesonide-loaded liposomes are linked to carrot cells via click chemistry to achieve budesonide-loaded carrot cells, which are validated to maintain stable and decrease the drug distribution and absorption in stomach and small intestine, while disintegrated by local microbiota after reaching colon to allow colon-targeting release. The glucocorticoid drug, intrinsic anti-inflammation substances in plant cells and the short-chain fatty acids generated by cell wall enzymatic degradation work synergistically to strengthen the therapeutic efficacy in ulcerative colitis mice models. This work provides insights into the development of plant-based drug excipients and offers an alternative strategy for the targeted treatment of colonic diseases.

title: Eco-evolutionary dynamics of active virus-host interactions in a freshwater lake revealed through metaHi-C
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Detecting active phage–bacteria interactions in natural microbial communities remains a major limitation for understanding their ecological dynamics and associated co-evolutionary processes. Here, we apply metaHi-C, a chromosome conformation capture method, to resolve active virus–host associations in a freshwater microbial community. From >900 microbial and >33,000 viral Hi-C–assembled genomes, we identify 100 high-confidence phage–host linkages spanning major freshwater bacterial lineages, including Limnohabitans, Acidimicrobium, Synechococcus, Candidatus Nanopelagicus, Candidatus Planktophila, Candidatus Methylopumilus, and Polynucleobacter. The inferred networks reveal signatures consistent with diverse infection patterns, including broad-host-range phages, cellular-level co-infection, kill-the-winner-like dynamics, and one-to-one interactions. These ecological patterns are associated with signatures of diversifying selection in host-interaction genes, consistent with host-range expansion, alongside conserved genomic regions in broad-host-range and co-infecting phages, indicating functional constraints on essential infection modules. Together, these results demonstrate that metaHi-C enables the direct detection of active phage–host associations within a community snapshot, and that, when combined with longitudinal metagenomic recruitment analyses, this approach can link community-level infection dynamics to underlying evolutionary processes, revealing how these forces shape population dynamics of freshwater bacteria.

title: ORE1 stabilizes PIF4 protein through a UBP12/UBP13-dependent regulatory module in thermomorphogenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding how plants integrate developmental programs with temperature-responsive growth remains a central challenge in plant biology. Here, we uncover a mechanism by which a canonical leaf senescence regulator directly governs thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis. We show that ORESARA1 (ORE1), best known for orchestrating leaf senescence, promotes warm temperature-induced hypocotyl and petiole elongation and the expression of warmth-responsive genes IAA19 and YUC8. Mechanistically, ORE1 acts upstream of PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 4 (PIF4), the central transcriptional hub for thermomorphogenesis. ORE1 does not alter PIF4 transcript abundance but specifically stabilizes PIF4 protein under warmth by physically interacting with PIF4 in the nucleus to enhance its deubiquitination. We identify the deubiquitinase UBP12/UBP13 as an essential component of this pathway; however, PIF4 does not bind UBP12/UBP13 directly. Biochemical and genetic analyses demonstrate that ORE1 functions as a molecular scaffold, recruiting PIF4 to an ORE1-UBP12/UBP13 complex to position UBP12/UBP13 for PIF4 deubiquitination. This UBP12/UBP13-ORE1-PIF4 module establishes a paradigm where a senescence factor regulates thermomorphogenesis by orchestrating deubiquitinase-mediated tuning of PIF4 proteostasis.

title: A multimodal ultrasound foundation model for diagnosis of unexplained lymphadenopathy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Unexplained lymphadenopathy (ULA) leads to delayed diagnosis and increases the risk of disease progression due to the absence of specific clinical symptoms and indicative medical history during early stages, thereby increasing reliance on invasive biopsy. Existing ultrasound artificial intelligence approaches mainly use single-modality static images, limiting their generalizability and clinical applicability. Here, we develop and validate a multimodal model integrating B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler flow imaging, ultrasound elastography, contrast-enhanced ultrasound videos, and clinical data for benign-malignant differentiation, etiologic stratification, and metastatic-origin prediction. This observational study includes both retrospective and prospective cohorts and uses a total of 154,740 multimodal keyframe images from 6,549 patients with pathologically confirmed lymphadenopathy across seven Chinese centers and 11 scanner manufacturers. The model shows robust performance across internal, external, device-heterogeneity, and reader study cohorts, outperforms senior radiologists across hierarchical tasks, and improves radiologists’ diagnostic performance across experience levels with model assistance, supporting its potential for noninvasive, efficient, and clinically aligned diagnosis of ULA.

title: A leptin receptor–LRP1 complex in the choroid plexus and tanycytes mediates leptin entry into the mouse brain
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Obesity is characterized by central leptin resistance, in which elevated circulating leptin fails to reach or activate its hypothalamic targets. Yet the mechanisms that mediate leptin transport into the brain remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that in the choroid plexus (ChP), leptin promotes the physical coupling of the leptin receptor (LepR) and low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein-1 (LRP1) to form a functional LRP1–LepR complex. Deletion of LepR or LRP1 in Foxj1-expressing cells, which include ChP epithelial cells and hypothalamic tanycytes, disrupts leptin entry into the brain, impairs hypothalamic leptin signaling, and induces hyperphagia and obesity. Intracerebroventricular leptin restores the anorexigenic response, confirming that the defect is in transport rather than central signaling. In diet-induced obese mice, formation of the LRP1–LepR complex is impaired, contributing to leptin resistance. These findings identify the LRP1–LepR complex in the ChP and tanycytes as an essential gateway for leptin entry into the brain and a potential therapeutic target in obesity.

title: A Dual-Crosslinked Coating with a Stable Self-generating Hydrogel Surface and Suppressed Water Permeation for Intrinsic Marine Antifouling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract To address the challenge of simultaneously achieving optimal antifouling efficacy and service durability for hydrogel coatings, dual-crosslinkable coatings were facilely fabricated from a polyacrylate bearing three functional groups (trimethoxysilyl, triisopropylsilyl ester, and ethyl acetoacetate groups) and a blended curing agent (amino-silane and branched polyethyleneimine). Upon seawater immersion, the coatings could rapidly self-generate an underwater superoleophobic surface characterized by hydrogel or porous structures, depending on their composition. Remarkably, the optimized coating (T14K14A14/15%P) maintained its hydrogel layer at the surface during 30 d of both static and dynamic immersion tests, indicating suppressed water permeation and hydrolysis within the coating and hence outstanding durability in service. This behavior was attributed to the barrier effect of the dense dual-crosslinked networks and the osmotic potential of the salt-entrapped hydrogel layer. Although no antifouling agent was incorporated, the T14K14A14/15%P coating exhibited an initial sterilization rate above 99%, which remained above 90% after 30 d of immersion, with protein and algal adhesion reductions of 93.5 and 93.1%, respectively. Through direct immersion and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, the coating also demonstrated decent anticorrosion performance even after long-term immersion, further verifying the suppressed water permeation. This work provides a strategy for designing durable hydrogel antifouling coatings without compromising antifouling performance.

title: Revealing Decomposition Pathways of an Ethylene Carbonate-Based Electrolyte with Fiber-Optic FTIR in NCM811 Li-Ion Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ni-rich NCM811 cathode is critical for achieving high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) but its instability issue at high potentials vs Li/Li+ remains unresolved. Mechanical degradation and lattice oxygen release of NCM811 could trigger nonequilibrium interfacial side reactions, including electrolyte oxidation, interphase evolution, and impedance growth. Understanding these processes is essential for the rational design of stable high-voltage electrolytes compatible with NCM811 cathodes. Here, we combine operando fiber-optic absorption mid-infrared Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy with a customized three-electrode NCM811|graphite full cell to track the evolution of an 1.5 M LiPF6/ethylene carbonate (EC) electrolyte during the formation cycles. Our analyses reveal that the EC carbonyl and PF6– -associated bands exhibit a synchronous maximum attenuation rate near 3.8 V vs Li/Li+, indicating coupled perturbation of the salt–solvent coordination environment. EC-derived ring-opening products and phosphorus-containing intermediates continue to accumulate during discharge, while reactive fluorophosphorus species undergo restructuring accompanied by the formation of oxidized carbonyl products during the subsequent constant-voltage charge. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy further shows that the increase in cell impedance originates predominantly from the NCM811 cathode rather than the graphite anode. These findings establish an isolated electrode–electrolyte interfacial framework for understanding coupled electrolyte decomposition in Ni-rich full cells and provide mechanistic insights into electrolyte/interface engineering for high-energy-density LIBs.

title: Synchronous Thermochromic and Heat-Response-Enhanced Anisotropic Conductive Janus Film Functionalized by Upconverting Luminescence for Multi-Scenario Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing stimulus-responsive multifunctional materials for multi-scenarios is meaningful. Herein, synchronous thermochromic and heat-response-enhanced anisotropic conductive Janus films (STHACJFs) are first designed and fabricated by respectively utilizing Janus-nanofiber and composite-nanofiber as microscopic building units to form the down-layer heat-response-enhanced anisotropic conductive Janus-nanofibers array membranes (HACJAMs) and up-layer thermochromic composite-nanofibers array membranes (TCAMs) of Janus films via electrospinning. Thermochromic transition temperatures of TCAMs are innovatively designed to match with response temperatures of HACJAMs, thereby enabling synchronous thermochromism and conductive anisotropy enhancement under single-temperature stimulation. The Janus-nanofiber with two micro-partitions endows HACJAMs with high conductive anisotropy and strong luminescence. An innovative strategy combining the phase transition-enhanced conductivity of W-doped VO2 with the intrinsic conductivity of polyaniline (PANI) is proposed to enhance the conductive anisotropy degree upon heating, and response temperatures of HACJAMs are regulated by adjusting W atomic percentages to tune the phase transition temperatures of W-doped VO2. Upon heating to 60, 55, and 45 °C, W-doped VO2 and PANI synergistically enhance the conductivity along the length direction of Janus-nanofiber, and the introduction of Na3ZrF7: Yb3+, Er3+ endows intense insulating capability in the diameter direction, realizing a heat-response-enhanced anisotropic conduction (ca. 105) in HACJAMs, while TCAMs exhibit distinct color transitions from pink, blue, and green to white at these temperatures, respectively. Both HACJAMs and TCAMs exhibit red upconverting luminescence under 980 nm laser excitation. By virtue of their superior multifunctionality, STHACJFs enable low-voltage electrical interconnection and dual-mode temperature indication in multi-temperature scenarios in a newly designed transistor switch circuit. Furthermore, STHACJFs demonstrate various applications, including transient thermal printing, temperature monitoring, static and dynamic anti-counterfeiting, temperature-controlled password recognition, and multilevel and multimodal information encryption. This research advances new anisotropic conductive membranes and stimulus-responsive multifunctional nanostructured materials.

title: Strategic autonomy and the energy transition: Rethinking Europe's geopolitical alignment
abstract: Europe's geopolitical alignment, its enduring deference to a US-led unipolar order, has come at the expense of its energy security and its ability to carry out the energy transition. This paper argues that greater strategic autonomy, the capacity and willingness to make economic and foreign policy decisions according to its own interests, would allow Europe to pursue both goals more effectively. It develops this argument in four parts. First, it characterises Europe's geopolitical alignment as a pattern of deference to US strategic priorities, sustained despite mounting costs to Europe's material interests, its standing and the multilateral order it claims to uphold. Second, it traces how this alignment shaped Europe's response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, contributing to a partly self-inflicted energy crisis followed by an abrupt and costly pivot to American liquefied natural gas that failed to resolve Europe's energy dependency. Third, it argues that on the energy transition Europe's interests are more closely aligned with Beijing's than with Washington's, although closer engagement deepens its dependence on Chinese clean technologies and critical raw materials. Europe should manage this trade-off by maintaining its de-risking approach and extending it to all its strategic dependencies, including those on the US. Finally, it argues that Europe will be unable to recalibrate its alignment and exercise strategic autonomy without building up its industrial and technological capacities and increasing its investment. Europe's choices will help determine the pace of the global energy transition, and with it, the world's chances of meeting its climate goals.

title: Unlocking public EV charging flexibility for grid balancing: A year-long empirical assessment of unidirectional and bidirectional smart charging in Prague
abstract: The transition of imbalance settlement in the Continental Europe synchronous area to 15-minute market time units, together with rising shares of variable renewable generation, raises the operational value of sub-hourly demand-side flexibility. Electric vehicles at public charging stations are an attractive source, yet empirical estimates of the balancing value of public smart charging remain scarce. This paper quantifies the technical potential of aggregated public smart charging in Prague to absorb the 15-minute system imbalance of the Czech transmission system operator ČEPS, using a full year of real charging-session data: 286,492 sessions across 1051 charging points. An ex-post optimization on a session-level flexibility envelope evaluates four configurations: the unidirectional (V1G) and bidirectional (V2G) operating modes, each under two user-comfort scenarios in which the delivered energy is preserved exactly (S1) or relaxed to the greater of 80% of it or 30 kWh (S2). The fleet’s uncontrolled load is removed first, so the same energy is re-timed, not added. Public V1G absorbs 4.44% of the imbalance energy under S1 and 4.85% under S2; V2G absorbs 7.09% and 7.64%. Bidirectional operation increases the absorbed energy by more than half, whereas relaxing comfort adds only about half a percentage point, so the bidirectional-infrastructure axis carries far more value than the user-incentive axis. These figures are a best-case ceiling computed with hindsight, not an operational forecast; valued at Czech final settlement prices, the V2G potential is a gross avoided balancing cost of up to about EUR 480,000 per year.

title: Autonomous AI-Robotics Design of High-Entropy Catalysts for the Urea Oxidation Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The combinatorial complexity inherent to high-entropy systems hinders the trial-and-error discovery of high-performance catalysts. Herein, we report an autonomous closed-loop workflow integrating retrieval-grounded knowledge mining, theory-informed machine learning, reliability-aware compositional screening, and robotic high-throughput experimentation for high-entropy Prussian blue analogue (PBA) urea oxidation reaction (UOR) catalysts. Large language models are employed for semantic reasoning and retrieval-grounded candidate generation within a structured evidence evaluation framework, with human scientific judgment incorporated in problem formulation, protocol calibration, and experimental prioritization. A theory-experiment hybrid model, together with applicability-domain and multilevel uncertainty analyses, enabled fine-grained screening of the quinary compositional space. Robotic validation of 40 performance- and reliability-prioritized compositions identified Fe0.11Co0.35Ni0.33Mn0.16Zn0.05-PBA as the best-performing composition under the standardized synthesis protocol, achieving a low UOR potential of 1.371 V at 10 mA cm–2. In a flow-cell UOR-assisted hydrogen evolution cell, this anode paired with a Pt/C cathode reached 100 mA cm–2 at 1.352 V and stably operated for 300 h at 0.5 A cm–2. This integrated workflow provides a practical and reliability-aware approach for navigating complex multicomponent material spaces through coordinated knowledge mining, theory-informed prediction, and autonomous experimental validation.

title: Data-Driven Electrolyte Design by Electrotopological State Descriptors for Na-Ion Batteries with Minimal Solid-Electrolyte Interphase Dissolution
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) determines the cycling reversibility of Na-ion batteries (NIBs). However, the high solubility of the Na-SEI continuously depletes the limited Na inventory in full cells, leading to accelerated electrolyte consumption and rapid capacity loss. To date, no general electrolyte design principles have been established to mitigate SEI dissolution, plaguing high Na-ion reversibility as an unsolved challenge. Herein, we quantitatively evaluate SEI dissolution across a broad range of NIB electrolytes and employ a closed-loop data-driven approach to correlate the dissolution behavior with over 200 electrolyte physicochemical descriptors. Among them, the solvent average electrotopological state (EState) index shows the strongest correlation with the SEI solubility. Guided by this insight, we designed high-EState electrolytes that suppressed SEI dissolution to only 6% of that in conventional electrolytes. The resulting minimal Na loss enabled a near-unity average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% over 1000 cycles in a hard carbon||NaMn0.33Fe0.33Ni0.33O2 full cell with all earth-abundant materials, successfully extending the End-of-Life battery model to Na-ion chemistry. This work elucidates quantitative correlations between electrolyte physicochemical properties and SEI dissolution, proposes EState-based electrolyte design principles with enhanced electrode–electrolyte interphase stability, and provides fundamental guidance to interphase designs for sustainable NIBs with high reversibility.

title: Highly Crystalline Triptycene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving high crystallinity in three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains a fundamental challenge, particularly beyond 4-connected tetrahedral nodes toward higher-connectivity building units. Here, we report the rapid synthesis of three highly crystalline triptycene-based COFs (COF-563, −564, and −565) as well-faceted, micrometer-sized crystals under mild conditions within 24 h. By employing rigid 6-connected trigonal prismatic triptycene-based building units, hexakis(4-aminophenyl/4-formylphenyl)triptycene (Trip-NH2/Trip-CHO), we access a topological regime of three-dimensional (3D) COFs that includes the established hea and stp nets as well as an unprecedented (6,6)-connected htp topology. These frameworks are constructed through reticulation of the triptycene nodes with tetrahedral (tetra(4-anilyl)methane (TAM)), rectangular (pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetraaniline (PyTTA)), and hexagonal (hexakis(4′-formyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)benzene (HFBB)) complementary linkers to yield the hea, stp, and htp structures, respectively. The resulting materials exhibit permanent porosity with Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface areas of up to 3769 m2 g–1─approaching a 2-fold increase over previously reported values for related topologies─and thermal stability up to 500 °C. This work establishes a versatile platform for the rapid formation of highly crystalline 3D organic frameworks and provides a blueprint for designing complex, highly porous architectures with controlled topology.

title: Conjugation Relay Beyond Local Coordination Rebalances Oxygen Intermediate Binding at Paired Cobalt Sites
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Correlated adsorption of oxygenated intermediates at single-metal sites limits the independent regulation of elementary steps in the oxygen reduction reaction. Herein, we establish a conjugation relay that tunes a structurally conserved cobalt pair through its molecular framework and carbon interface. We construct a pyrolysis-free series comprising a dicobalt complex and two conjugated coordination polymers grown directly on Ketjen Black, progressively extending the π network while retaining comparable Co2N4O2 pockets and cobalt loadings. Microscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support comparable cobalt pairing and local coordination across the series. Comparisons with unsupported counterparts and a physical mixture help distinguish molecular conjugation, direct interfacial coupling, and conductive contact. Spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that molecular π extension redistributes charge around the cobalt pair and that carbon coupling amplifies this response. Within the paired pocket, *OOH spans both cobalt centers, whereas *OH remains bound primarily to one center. These distinct geometries cause their adsorption free energies to respond unequally, decreasing the ΔG*OOH – ΔG*OH offset from the 3.13 eV single-site reference to 2.62 eV for the most conjugated supported model. Potential-dependent infrared spectroscopy detects *OOH at more positive potentials as conjugation increases, supporting facilitated formation under reaction conditions. The most conjugated catalyst delivers an iR-corrected half-wave potential of 1.02 V, with only a 13 mV loss after 30,000 cycles. These findings establish conjugation beyond local coordination as a molecular design strategy for relaxing adsorption-energy correlations at multiatom catalytic sites.
