title: Topology‐Encoded Polymer Networks for Thermo‐Responsive Wrinkling With Dynamic Diffraction Tunability
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermo‐responsive wrinkles provide a scalable route to adaptive optical surfaces. However, achieving thermally tunable structural color with high diffraction efficiency remains challenging, limiting their applications in optical devices and information encryption. This challenge arises from conventional wrinkle systems relying on empirical macroscopic parameters and lacking molecular‐level design principles based on network topology. Herein, we propose a crosslinker chain‐length programming strategy to construct thermally responsive optical wrinkled surfaces with encoded polymer network topology. By tuning bismaleimide crosslinker chain length, network topology and thermomechanical response are regulated, directing thermally induced surface instability into oriented periodic wrinkles with programmable structural color and diffraction efficiency. Using crosslinker chain length and prestrain as design variables, a two‐dimensional diffraction efficiency design map is constructed to delineate diffractive and non‐diffractive regimes, achieving a maximum diffraction efficiency of 22.7%. Chain length‐dependent UV‐induced maleimide dimerization enables spatially resolved orthogonal patterning, allowing hidden information to be written and read out optically under manual stretching without external devices. Dynamic Diels–Alder (D–A) reversibility supports partial wrinkle amplitude erasure, enabling post‐read information invalidation. This study bridges molecularly encoded polymer network topology and macroscopic optical performance, providing molecular‐level design principles for multistimuli‐responsive optical platforms and advanced anti‐counterfeiting materials.

title: Nonclassical Electrostriction: The Insights From X‐Ray Absorption Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Nonclassical electrostriction (NCES) has emerged in a growing class of ionic solids that exhibit electromechanical responses far exceeding predictions of the conventional Newnham scaling law despite moderate dielectric permittivity and high elastic modulus. Unlike classical electrostriction, which is associated with nearly uniform anharmonic deformation of the crystal lattice, NCES originates from the field‐induced reorganization of a small population of locally distorted structural units. This Review examines the unique role of x‐ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy in identifying the electromechanically active structural units, resulting in the understanding of atomistic mechanisms underlying this behavior. Element‐specific x‐ray absorption near edge structure and extended XAFS (EXAFS) measurements identify local symmetry breaking, defect‐associated elastic dipoles, multimodal bond‐length distributions, and strongly anharmonic bonds that remain “hidden” from average‐structure probes. Field‐modulated, high energy resolution, and differential XAFS further isolate the minority structural units directly responsible for macroscopic strain. Aliovalent and isovalent dopants are shown to produce distinct microscopic mechanisms, involving vacancy‐associated static and dynamic elastic dipoles, respectively, embedding strong attributes of anharmonicity. These results establish local structure and bond dynamics as key descriptors of NCES and highlight in situ, stimulus‐modulated XAFS as a powerful route for uncovering and ultimately controlling electromechanical coupling in defect‐engineered materials.

title: Learning to Program Dimple‐Encoded Strips for Morphing Architectures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Programmable morphing structures that translate local mechanical states into global shape transformations enable deployable, adaptive, and reconfigurable systems. Dimple‐encoded elastic strips provide a minimal platform in which arrays of bistable dimples can collectively program large bending deformation. Yet the nonlinear mapping from the encoded geometry to the final configuration makes inverse design challenging. Here, we report a learning‐enabled strategy for programming dimple‐encoded strips with prescribed morphing profiles and using them as building blocks for higher‐level morphing architectures. Finite‐element simulations are converted into centerline‐based tangent‐field representations to train a one‐dimensional convolutional neural‐network surrogate that maps local dimple encoding and strip geometry to global shape. The trained surrogate enables gradient‐based inverse design of target morphologies, with optimized designs validated by independent simulations and physical prototypes. Variable‐width strip modules expand the accessible shape space and enable width‐conditioned curvature programming. Rotational tessellation of programmed strip modules creates dome‐like morphing shells, while hierarchical integration of curvature‐programmed strips with folding modules yields an artifical flower exhibiting sequential opening through dimple switching. These results establish dimple‐encoded strips as learnable building blocks that connect local bistable encoding, inverse design, and hierarchical shape formation, providing a route toward task‐specific morphing components for soft robotics, adaptive interfaces, and deployable structures.

title: Self‐Assembled Nanoplatform for Modulating the ATP‐Adenosine Pathway and CD8+ T Cell Metabolism to Potentiate Radiotherapy‐Mediated Antitumor Immunity
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Radiotherapy (RT) is one of the primary clinical modalities for tumor treatment, yet its therapeutic efficacy is restricted by post‐RT immunosuppression and impaired function of tumor‐infiltrating cytotoxic T lymphocytes. Herein, we fabricate self‐assembled nanoparticles based on sodium metatungstate (POM1) and spermidine (Spd), followed by polyethylene glycol (PEG) modification to enhance biocompatibility (denoted as POM1‐Spd/PEG). Structural characterization and molecular simulations confirm that the core POM1‐Spd complex is assembled via electrostatic and van der Waals interactions, with each POM1 cluster stably anchoring two Spd molecules to form a dimeric supramolecular architecture. Benefiting from these weak intermolecular interactions, POM1‐Spd/PEG can efficiently disassemble in the weakly acidic tumor microenvironment to release free POM1 and Spd. Notably, we uncover that POM1 possesses unrecognized dual functional properties, which act as both a potent radiosensitizer to amplify RT‐induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) and an efficient CD39 inhibitor that prevents the conversion of ICD‐released ATP to immunosuppressive adenosine (ADO), thereby reversing ADO‐mediated tumor immunosuppression and sustaining robust antitumor immune activation. Furthermore, the released Spd upregulates fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial ATP synthesis in CD8 + T cells, consequently boosting their proliferation and cytotoxic effector functions. When combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors, this strategy can effectively trigger systemic antitumor immunity to further enhance therapeutic efficacy and suppress the growth and metastasis of distant tumors. Collectively, our work develops a distinctive self‐assembled nanoplatform capable of achieving radiosensitization, regulating the ATP‐ADO pathway, and improving CD8 + T cell metabolism, offering a promising approach to amplify RT efficacy by remodeling antitumor immunity.

title: Bioinspired Membrane Fusion–Gated Hydrogel Biosensor for Extraction‐Free Viral RNA Detection of Infectious Influenza Virus
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Emerging infectious diseases driven by zoonotic spillover demand rapid and reliable molecular diagnostics for pathogen identification and surveillance. However, conventional nucleic acid diagnostics cannot distinguish infectious virions from nonviable RNA fragments, limiting infectivity‐resolved virus identification. Here, we report a bioinspired membrane‐coated hydrogel (Memgel) sensor that enables extraction‐free molecular detection of influenza virus while distinguishing fusion‐competent virions from noninfectious viral material. The platform integrates a cell‐mimetic supported lipid bilayer with a polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogel matrix encapsulating recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) reagents. Under endosome‐mimicking acidic conditions, hemagglutinin‐mediated membrane fusion selectively delivers viral genomic RNA from infectious virions into the hydrogel matrix, triggering sequence‐specific amplification while suppressing signals from free viral RNA fragments. As a proof of concept, the Memgel sensor was evaluated for the detection of influenza A (H9N2) in simulated nasal fluid and raw milk matrices, achieving a limit of detection of 10 1.23 TCID 50 mL − 1 while maintaining robust detection performance without RNA extraction. Coupled with a portable fluorescence reader, the system demonstrates compatibility with compact fluorescence‐based readout for future point‐of‐care implementation. This fusion‐gated sensing strategy provides a materials‐based framework for infectivity‐resolved molecular diagnostics of emerging viral pathogens.

title: Metal‐Chelating Molecule‐Enabled Multidentate Molecular Bridge Engineering of the Buried Interface for High‐Performance Fully Printed Carbon‐Based Perovskite Solar Modules
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon‐based perovskite solar modules (C‐PSMs) provide a scalable and metal‐electrode‐free platform for stable perovskite photovoltaics, yet their efficiencies remain constrained by defective and mechanically fragile buried SnO 2 /perovskite interfaces. Conventional interfacial modifiers generally rely on limited coordination, making it difficult to simultaneously achieve robust passivation and strong interfacial adhesion. Here, we introduce two metal‐chelating molecules to construct multidentate molecular bridges at the buried interface in C‐PSMs. Diglycine disodium (DDS), although capable of coordinating with both SnO 2 and perovskite, exhibits weak configurational selectivity because multiple interfacial coordination modes are energetically accessible, preventing stable bilateral bridge formation. In contrast, tetrasodium iminodisuccinate (IDS) coordinates with both SnO 2 and perovskite, constructing a robust bilateral molecular bridge, suppressing interfacial defects, enhancing charge transfer, and interfacial adhesion. Consequently, the fully printed 30 × 30 cm 2 IDS C‐PSMs achieve a record efficiency of 19.26% with an active area of 563.78 cm 2 (certified 18.04%, with a mask‐defined area of 487.6 cm 2 ), which represents the highest reported PCE for a device of this size and architecture. The unencapsulated IDS C‐PSM retains over 90% of its initial efficiency after 1130 h of maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C and over 85% after 2184 h under damp‐heat conditions (85°C and 85% RH).

title: Enhanced Molecular‐Structure Dual‐Recognition by Enzyme‐Embedded Metal‐Phenolic Networks for Wearable Plant Sensing of Pesticides
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT On‐site monitoring of plant health using enzyme‐based wearable sensors is essential for sustainable agriculture, yet inherent enzyme instability and poor molecular recognition remain major obstacles. Here, we present a robust plant‐wearable hydrogel sensor based on an acetylcholinesterase‐embedded metal‐phenolic network (AChE@MPN) to overcome these limitations through a dual‐recognition strategy, markedly improving stability and selectivity relative to conventional sensors. The MPN protects the enzyme's native conformation, maintaining catalytic kinetics comparable to those of the free enzyme. Within this architecture, the dual‐recognition strategy integrates metal‐assisted adsorption with enzymatic recognition, engaging pesticide molecules through synergistic P‐O‐Zr coordination, hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking to yield a 1.41‐fold higher response to phoxim than that obtained with free AChE. Notably, the AChE@MPN exhibits an approximately 88‐fold higher binding affinity for phoxim than for its nonaromatic analog malathion, indicating that the signal gain originates from selective enrichment. These features enable the sensor to discriminate phoxim from interfering substances, with a limit of detection of 2 ng mL −1 , and to perform on‐site monitoring of phoxim degradation on living tomato plants. This dual‐recognition design offers a general strategy for pesticide monitoring and may inspire plant‐sensing innovations for sustainable agriculture.

title: Quenching or Accelerating Large‐Scale Surface Reconstruction by the Lightest Element: Facet‐Dependent Hydrogen‐Induced Reconstruction (HIR)
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Adsorbate‐induced surface reconstruction is believed to be a critical determinant of catalyst performance under operando conditions. The Pd–Ag bimetallic catalyst, used industrially for selective acetylene hydrogenation, is thought to undergo hydrogen‐induced surface reconstruction (HIR) that exposes Pd active sites. However, the kinetic origin of HIR remains unknown because hydrogen is difficult to image. Here, using large‐scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we resolve the kinetics of H‐driven reconstruction. On Pd‐covered Ag surfaces, reconstruction initially involves Pd–Ag exchange at domain peripheries and Ag atoms popping up to encapsulate exposed Pd. This process is faster on (100) than on (111). Hydrogen suppresses reconstruction on (111) above 0.3 ML, but accelerates Pd dispersion and encapsulation on (100) mediated by transient Pd–H pair formation. This facet dependence arises from hydrogen‐induced kinetic hindrance of edge Pd diffusion away from Pd domains on (111). Analysis of MD‐derived surface structures further shows that the Pd3 triangular surface pattern favors selective acetylene hydrogenation, confirming HIR's role in determining active‐site structure. These findings provide the first evidence for facet‐dependent, large‐scale surface reconstruction induced by the lightest element and establish HIR as a key determinant of catalytic activity and selectivity.

title: Copper‐Catalyzed Enantioconvergent 1,4‐Difunctionalization of Homoallylic and Homopropargylic Alcohols via Radical‐Relay Deoxygenation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the long‐recognized structural diversity and accessibility of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols as synthetic building blocks, their deoxygenative radical difunctionalization remains a formidable challenge due to the lack of a linkage strategy integrating the respective functionalization of non‐adjacent hydroxyl and alkene/alkyne groups. Herein, we present an efficient platform for the deoxygenative radical 1,4‐difunctionalization of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols through an unprecedented remote hydrogen atom transfer‐triggered radical‐relay deoxygenation process. Utilizing 1,3‐benzodithiolylium as an effective hydroxyl‐activating reagent, copper‐catalyzed enantioconvergent 1,4‐perfluoroalkylamidation and 1,4‐cyanoperfluoroalkylation have been achieved with excellent regio‐ and enantioselectivity.

title: Fast‐Discharge‐Induced Non‐Equilibrium Phase Transition in Ni‐Rich Layered Oxide Cathode at High Voltage
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid adoption of electric vehicles necessitates lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) that can sustain extreme fast charging (XFC) without rapid degradation. Ni‐rich layered cathodes deliver high energy density, yet their poor stability under high‐rate operation limits practical deployment and the mechanistic origin of fast capacity decay remains poorly understood. Here, using high time‐resolved operando XRD, together with theoretical analyses, we reveal that a rate‐dependent non‐equilibrium H3→H2 phase transition under rapid discharge (≥4 C) induces huge lattice displacement and nanoscale strain, which significantly lower the migration barrier for Ni, thereby promoting irreversible rock‐salt phase formation and structural collapse. Importantly, guided by this mechanistic understanding, we propose a cycling protocol introducing a brief low‐rate discharge step at high voltage (4.5 V→4.0 V), which effectively suppresses the detrimental H2+H3 phase separation and generation of internal stress. Compared to that of the cell under constant high cycling rates (6 C), the capacity retention improves 29% for the one with optimized discharge procedure after 1000 cycles. These results clarify the underneath electrochemical–mechanical degradation behavior of Ni‐rich layered cathodes at different rates (1/3 C, 1 C, 4 C, and 6 C), providing practical guidance for designing durable batteries with superior fast‐charging abilities.

title: Heteroatom‐Modulated Aggregation of Diketopyrrolopyrrole Derivatives by Single‐Atom Substitution to Construct NIR‐II‐Absorbing Photothermal Agents With Over 90% Efficiency
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic small‐molecule photothermal materials with second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) absorption have attracted enormous interest for biomedical applications, yet simultaneously achieving strong NIR‐II absorption and high photothermal conversion efficiency remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report to conduct the heteroatom‐modulated aggregation of diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) derivatives (named as DAQ‐T and DAQ‐Fu) by single‐atom substitution to construct high‐performance NIR‐II‐absorbing photothermal agents. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that oxygen‐for‐sulfur substitution precisely modulates electrostatic potential distributions and tailors intermolecular π–π interactions by leveraging the distinct electronegativities of chalcogens, driving a transformation from H ‐aggregation in DAQ‐T to J ‐aggregation in DAQ‐Fu. The resulting J ‐aggregated DAQ‐Fu nanoparticles feature a distinct absorption band at 1064 nm with a molar extinction coefficient of 3.26 × 10 4 L mol −1 cm −1 , and exhibit an outstanding photothermal conversion efficiency of 92.4%. This photothermal effect exerts potent antitumor efficacy by regulating apoptosis and immune‐related signaling pathways, enabling the synergy of photothermal therapy and as‐induced immunogenic cell death to suppress both primary and distant tumors growth with about 90% and 63% inhibition rates, respectively, under biocompatible irradiation. This work demonstrates atom‐precise aggregation modulation, offering a promising pathway to engineer NIR‐II‐absorbing organic small‐molecule photothermal agents for synergistic photothermal cancer immunotherapy.

title: Mechanism of Alkene Skeletal Isomerization in Zeolites Revealed by Coupled‐Cluster Accurate Free‐Energy Simulations
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The mechanism of Brønsted acid‐catalyzed transformations in zeolites is generally described in terms of carbocationic intermediates, yet their thermodynamic stability and mechanistic role remain controversial. Resolving this issue requires chemically accurate free‐energy simulations, which are beyond the reach of conventional density functional theory (DFT) and prohibitively expensive at the coupled‐cluster level. Here, we combine a cluster‐based QM/QM ‐learning strategy with a machine‐learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to enable molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with near‐CCSD(T) accuracy. Applied to the skeletal isomerization of n ‐butene in chabazite, the resulting free‐energy surfaces (FESs) reveal a mechanistic picture that differs qualitatively from that predicted by generalized‐gradient approximation (GGA) functionals. Rather than proceeding through persistent carbocationic intermediates, the reaction is governed by a cascade of highly transient ionic configurations, while protonated methylcyclopropane (PMCP) is identified as a short‐lived reactive configuration rather than a genuine metastable intermediate. These findings provide a more physically consistent description of one of the prototypical reactions in zeolite catalysis. More generally, the methodology introduced here provides a practical route toward chemically accurate free‐energy simulations of heterogeneous catalytic reactions involving highly reactive charged species, opening the way to quantitative mechanistic studies of complex catalytic processes.

title: The Self‐Powered Nanofiltration Membrane Driven by Pulsed Pressure for Efficient Selective Separation of Na+/Ca2+
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Enhancing electrostatic repulsion against divalent cations in the selective layer is effective in improving monovalent/divalent cation separation in nanofiltration. However, conventional grafting and coating strategies are limited by insufficient reaction sites or poor coating stability, both of which restrict further improvements in monovalent/divalent cation selectivity. Herein, a positively charged nanofiltration membrane with a piezoelectric response (PQNF) was designed via reverse thermally induced phase separation (RTIPS) coupled with interfacial polymerization (IP). RTIPS endowed the poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) substrate with a sponge‐like pore structure, a narrow pore‐size distribution, and a high β ‐phase content. Subsequently, the PQNF membrane was prepared via IP, quaternization, and corona poling. Under pulsed pressure operation, a periodic in situ voltage of 0.4 V was generated, which contributed to the 98.7% Ca 2+ rejection and a Na + /Ca 2+ separation factor of 89.6. The membrane also maintained stable separation performance over 144 h and showed enhanced antifouling performance under pulsed pressure operation in a 14 h fouling test. Finally, an “electrostatic–piezoelectric synergistic enhancement” separation mechanism was proposed and supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

title: Solvation‐Directed Electric Double Layer Formation in Low‐Concentration Electrolytes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The electric double layer (EDL) governs interfacial stability in lithium metal batteries, yet its rational design remains constrained by concentrated electrolytes or complex solvent systems. Here we demonstrate that the EDL in low‐concentration electrolytes (LCEs) can be rationally programmed through anion selection based on their solvation behavior, decoupling interfacial stability from the heavy consumption of lithium salts and sophisticated solvent blends. By systematically screening anions with distinct Li + ‐anion coordination strengths and steric profiles, we formulate a mixed‐anion LCE and uncover a fundamental principle: large, weakly coordinatinganions (WCAs) accumulate at the interface to form a persistent charge‐shielding layer, whereas small, strongly coordinating anions (SCAs) are dynamically driven deeper into the Helmholtz region under polarization, where they actively modulate interfacial (de)solvation kinetics. This solvation‐defined division of labor creates a rationally designed, self‐adaptive EDL that couples electrostatic stabilization with interfacial chemistry. Beyond offering a high‐performance LCE formulation, this work establishes a direct and mechanistic linkage between bulk solvation architecture and interfacial EDL organization in dilute electrolytes, revealing that the EDL can itself be programmed through anion‐specific solvation motifs to dictate interfacial stability, introducing a design paradigm for materially efficient electrolyte engineering based on solvation‐directed EDL formation.

title: Metal–Backboned Architectures Enable Magneto–Spin–Charge Engineering for High–Performance Li–CO2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Simultaneous CO 2 conversion and high–energy–density energy storage are urgently needed for sustainable energy systems where Li–CO 2 batteries provide an ideal solution, yet their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish CO 2 redox kinetics. Emerging metal–backboned molecules, which contain numerous metal atoms as catalytically active sites, are expected to accelerate CO 2 reduction reaction kinetics due to their unique architectures and properties. Herein, we report a novel mixed–valence cobalt–backboned polymer with effective spin manipulation as an efficient electrocatalyst and conductive scaffold for Li–CO 2 batteries, which enables a low overpotential of 1.06 V and outstanding stable cycling over 2700 h. An external magnetic field drives Co centers from low–spin to high–spin configuration and enhances intermetallic intervalence charge transfer, synergistically strengthening CO 2 adsorption and activation by increasing unpaired electron orbital occupancy and facilitating electron transfer to CO 2 antibonding orbitals. This work establishes metal–backboned architectures as a versatile platform for spin–charge cooperative engineering, opening a new avenue for kinetically accelerated next–generation energy storage systems.

title: Manganese‐Catalyzed Electrochemical Nitrogenative‐Oxygenative Cleavage of Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a manganese‐catalyzed electrochemical nitrogenative‐oxygenative scission of olefins to nitriles and carbonyls. Mechanistic and kinetic studies reveal distinct precatalyst‐activation and productive‐turnover regimes, and support conversion of the manganese precursor into a mixed‐valent oxo‐bridged dimanganese(III/IV) species, followed by azide‐dependent formation of a product‐forming manganese species. Notably, polyunsaturated substrates can undergo alkene‐chemoselective cleavage with preferential reaction at the more substituted C═C bond, while the present protocol enables unprecedented reactivity towards activated and unactivated alkenes with broad functional‐group tolerance.

title: Electric‐Field‐Manipulated Reaction Pathway Engineering in Lupinus micranthus‐Like High‐Entropy Alloy Nanowires for Direct Alcohol Fuel Cells
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic alcohol oxidation in direct fuel cells is constrained by CO poisoning and insufficient hydroxyl generation at low potentials. Here we show that anisotropic PtFeCoIrRhCu high‐entropy alloy nanowires with Lupinus micranthus ‐like morphology generate a local electric field through coupling of strain‐induced lattice distortion with charge redistribution, enabling a directional capture‐migration‐dissociation relay of interfacial water for efficient low‐potential hydroxyl generation, in which H 2 O is preferentially captured at Fe/Co sites, migrates under field polarization, and dissociates at Rh/Ir sites. In situ infrared spectroscopy reveals that the electric field reorganizes interfacial water into a more ordered hydrogen‐bond network, facilitating water activation. Density functional theory calculations, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry and operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy further demonstrate that the generated hydroxyl species accelerate CO oxidative removal and promote the non‐CO oxidation pathway. Consequently, the catalyst achieves a methanol oxidation mass activity of 3.76 A mg Pt −1 , 8.36 times that of Pt/C, together with a direct methanol fuel cell peak power density of 163.06 mW cm −2 and stable membrane‐electrode operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm −2 . These findings establish strain–charge coupling as a general strategy for engineering interfacial water activation and directing reaction‐pathway selectivity in multimetallic electrocatalysts.

title: A risk-averse bidding and scheduling strategy for process industry VPPs in demand response markets based on thermodynamically-enhanced RTN
Technology trajectories and critical raw materials in sodium-ion battery innovation: An LLM-assisted patent analysis
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising complement to lithium-ion batteries for cost-sensitive and resource-resilient energy-storage applications. Despite growing technological and industrial interest, the structure of SIB innovation remains insufficiently understood because existing patent studies have largely focused on aggregate filing trends. To address this gap, this study develops a high-resolution patent landscape through large language model-assisted classification of 9670 patent families across technological domains, battery components, electrode material classes, assignee types, regions, and cathode-related critical raw materials. The results show that SIB innovation remains strongly materials-driven, with material-related inventions accounting for almost 86% of all patent families. Within this landscape, layered transition-metal oxides account for 51% of cathode-related patent families, while hard carbon represents 44% of anode-related patent families. Innovation activity is also highly concentrated geographically, with more than 94% of the analyzed patent families including at least one Chinese assignee. At the organizational level, companies focus more strongly on near-term material pathways, whereas public organizations show greater engagement with alternative chemistries. Furthermore, critical raw materials (CRMs) continue to play a central role in SIB cathodes: 76% of cathode patent families require at least one CRM, 15% include one conditionally, and only 9% contain no CRM. The degree of this exposure varies substantially across cathode classes, with manganese, nickel, phosphorus, and vanadium emerging as the most prominent CRMs. Overall, these findings show that the strategic value of SIBs depends on material selection, regional innovation capacity, and chemistry-specific CRM exposure, with implications for research, industry, and policy.

title: Operating-point-dependent power-flow linearisation for joint siting, sizing, and dispatch of long-duration energy storage in distribution grids
abstract: Long-term energy-storage planning in distribution grids involves long time series, non-linear network constraints, and mixed-integer siting and sizing decisions. Especially detailed AC formulations are computationally challenging for long optimisation horizons. To address this challenge, we propose an operating-point-dependent linearisation of the AC power-flow equations using sensitivity coefficients and integrating them into a mixed-integer linear program for the joint siting, sizing and dispatch of different flexibility options over long time horizons. An iterative AC power-flow validation and relinearisation procedure is used to ensure approximation accuracy. Different approaches to select the linearisation points are benchmarked, either by using each operating point or by clustering approaches, using k -medoids while retaining the original injection and network data. The method is evaluated on SimBench distribution networks and benchmarked against non-linear AC-OPF formulations. Operating-point-dependent linearisation enables computationally tractable storage planning over long time horizons while preserving detailed network information. Clustering can reduce computational effort by about 40 % , provided that the original operating-point data are retained. The linearised model deviates from the lossless AC-OPF benchmark by approximately 0.3 % in storage power and 0.6 % in energy capacity. To demonstrate the use of the method, we develop a case study where household flexibility and grid scale storage are co-optimised in a full-year planning problem. The results show that aggregate household flexibility primarily affects storage sizing, whereas its spatial distribution influences local grid conditions and optimal siting.

title: From one cycle to full life: Ultra-early battery degradation assessment for operational assessment and rapid screening
Stochastic assessment of eight emergency electricity supply configurations for urban shelters: Performance limits and the role of vehicle-to-shelter
abstract: Emergency electricity planning for urban shelters requires comparing heterogeneous supply resources under uncertain, time-varying demand. This study assesses eight specified emergency electricity-supply configurations, including two Vehicle-to-Shelter (V2S) arrangements, for a 1000-person shelter during a 72-h grid outage. A common framework combines paired Monte Carlo simulation, hourly supply–demand matching, continuous resource-state evolution, and access-conditioned variance decomposition, while retaining configuration-specific constraints on power, usable energy, infrastructure continuity, resource access, and deployment timing. Across nine demand and disaster-severity scenarios, adequacy declined as shelter services expanded and cold-season demand increased, while access-dependent resources were additionally constrained by infrastructure continuity, allocation, and arrival. High coverage of the specified diesel-generator configuration depended strongly on its usable energy in the most demanding scenario, where a 20% stock reduction lowered mean energy coverage ratio (ECR) from 0.819 to 0.659. Similar aggregate coverage also concealed different temporal risks. Under hot conditions with moderate disaster severity, a mobile power-supply truck and a local-plus-external V2S arrangement had nearly identical mean ECRs (0.368 and 0.367) under baseline access assumptions but different temporal shortfall patterns. The truck provided no support before allocation and arrival, whereas locally parked EVs supplied limited early power. Access-state differences accounted for most observed ECR variance for the access-dependent configurations in the two examined scenarios, distinguishing conditional resource capability from unconditional shelter adequacy. These findings support mechanism-based screening by power, endurance, immediate availability, and credible access arrangements, while suggesting a potential role for V2S as a conditional supplement rather than a universal substitute for dedicated backup supply.

title: A continental dilemma: Is centralized or decentralized renewable hydrogen cheaper?
abstract: Hydrogen is a strong candidate on the path towards the decarbonization of the transportation, energy, and industry sectors. In addition to being a well-known element, hydrogen is mainly produced from fossil fuels, with the renewable production chain still requiring development. In this context, this work evaluates the technical and economic potential of hydrogen production using solar photovoltaic (PV) energy and electricity purchased from the Brazilian grid, and evaluates two layouts: (i) centralized production of solar PV energy and hydrogen at the same site and (ii) decentralized production of energy and hydrogen powered by the Brazilian interconnected grid (SIN). The use of PV energy is found to decrease the levelized cost of hydrogen ( L C O H ) when compressed, from 14.00 USD / kg to 13.24 USD / kg in the centralized case and to 9.11 USD / kg in the decentralized case. However, a system powered only by P V energy had a cost of 18.23 USD / kg ; this corroborates the fact that the highest verified cost is from the purchase of energy from the grid. From the analysis of the design parameters, increasing the electrolyzer power and the size of the PV field reduces the L C O H , due to the economies of scale of both pieces of equipment. The optimization shows that it is possible to reach an L C O H for compressed hydrogen of 9.89 USD / kg for the centralized system and values of 5.88 USD / kg for the decentralized system.

title: Biodegradable Periodic Mesoporous Organosilica Nanoparticles for Enhanced Rifampicin Activity Against Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Its Biofilm
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant (MDR) and biofilm-associated bacterial infections are increasingly prevalent in healthcare settings, and they create a serious global health problem by increasing the morbidity and mortality rates. Nanomaterial-based alternative therapeutic approaches have therefore been widely explored as potential strategies for improving the treatment of MDR infections. Here, we report a drug delivery system based on biocompatible and biodegradable surface-engineered periodic mesoporous organosilica nanoparticles (nanoPMOs), designed to enhance the antibacterial and antibiofilm efficiency of the antibiotic rifampicin against the high-priority MDR Gram-negative pathogenic bacterium, Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Mannose functionalization appeared to improve the association of the nanoPMOs with bacterial cells and biofilms, while the acid-cleavable imine linkages enabled faster nanoparticle degradation and rifampicin release under acidic conditions. Compared with free rifampicin, the rifampicin-loaded nanoPMOs effectively killed planktonic bacteria and reduced the biomass of preformed biofilms under the tested in vitro conditions. The rifampicin-loaded nanoPMO formulations also showed low nonspecific cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity at the concentrations examined.

title: Traffic-scenario-recognition-based energy management strategy with variable prediction horizon for connected fuel cell buses

Comparative analysis of PV allocation rules in heterogeneous energy communities for collective self-consumption
abstract: This paper investigates how photovoltaic (PV) electricity allocation rules shape the technical, economic, and distributional performance of collective self-consumption schemes at both community and individual levels. A unified analytical framework is developed to compare four allocation mechanisms—static, hourly-variable, dynamic, and priority-based—across three community configurations: a prosumer-only community, an expanded community with fixed PV capacity, and an expanded community with PV capacity scaled to demand. The study is based on a real-case study of the CERCA energy community in Spain, using one year of measured hourly consumption, meteorological, and tariff data. Results show that allocation rules significantly influence both technical and economic outcomes. In the reference scenario, self-consumption ( SC ) rises from 0.39 to 0.41 (static, hourly-variable) to 0.45 (dynamic, priority), while IRR increases from 10.0% to 11.7% and payback decreases from 8.1 to 7.2 years. Community expansion with unchanged PV capacity improves local PV utilization, reaching SC values of 0.58–0.59, maximum IRR of 12.7% and payback of 6.7 years. At the individual level, priority allocation achieves the highest returns but the greatest dispersion of benefits (the coefficient of variation ( CV ) of individual SC is in the 20.7%–41.8% range), whereas dynamic allocation delivers comparable performance with a more balanced distribution ( CV of individual SC up to 9.2%). Sensitivity analysis shows that, for fixed PV capacity, profitability is maximized with 13–15 additional consumers, yielding an IRR of up to 13.3%. Overall, allocation rules are crucial in shaping both efficiency and equity in energy communities, with direct implications for policy and market design.

title: A probabilistic region-based model for evaluating the integrated hosting capacity of photovoltaics and electric vehicles in power distribution networks
A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-enhanced framework for knowledge-guided campus-scale building retrofit design
abstract: Urban-scale building envelope optimization is constrained by the computational burden of iterative simulation. This study proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced framework that replaces the search phase of conventional optimization: literature-screened envelope solutions are retrieved from a curated corpus and then cross-checked through physics-based EnergyPlus simulation, rather than located through exhaustive parametric search. The corpus comprises 20,247 initially identified publications screened to a core of 338 studies, together with an experimentally characterized database of 502 envelope materials, of which 65 were used in the assemblies evaluated here. A three-stage progressive retrofit strategy — conventional high-performance insulation; vacuum insulation panels, aerogel and phase change materials (PCMs); and optimized PCM hybrid assemblies — was applied to seven reference buildings on Yonsei University's 86-building campus in Seoul, Korea. A systematic literature review established that whole-building field-measured savings are systematically 0.25–0.75× of simulation-only upper bounds, a correction embedded directly in the retrieval thresholds and screening criteria. The seven reference buildings produce a simulated mean building-level EUI reduction of 21.5%, ranging from 9.5% in high window-to-wall-ratio modern buildings to 39.6% in thermally deficient heritage structures, while campus-wide analysis of all 86 buildings yields 15.7% (124.4 to 104.9 kWh/m 2 ·year). EnergyPlus models were not calibrated against sub-metered operational data, so all reported reductions are simulation-based screening estimates. The framework offers a scalable, computationally efficient route to envelope retrofit planning for large institutional portfolios and urban decarbonization programs.

title: Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance
abstract: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures interact with strategic infrastructure, political legitimacy and transition finance. The central argument is temporal: political commitments, infrastructure development and financing arrangements evolve at different speeds, generating misalignment between strategic ambitions and implementation capacity. Institutional risk compression is introduced as the governance mechanism through which socio-political durability, regulatory credibility and financial arrangements interact to contain or amplify uncertainty. The framework is explored through a case study of Sicily, a strategic Mediterranean energy node connecting North African gas corridors, renewable development, grid interconnections and prospective EU–Africa energy partnerships. Evidence on infrastructure investment, renewable permitting and cross-border financing illustrates how geopolitical priorities interact with territorial distributional tensions, regulatory constraints and investment conditions. The analysis highlights three interconnected challenges: aligning commitments across different time horizons, reconciling system-wide infrastructure benefits with local legitimacy and distinguishing genuine risk reduction from the redistribution of financial exposure. The paper contributes a framework for understanding how geopolitical pressures are transmitted through regional energy transitions and identifies implications for EU energy security, infrastructure governance and transition finance.

Terminal Ligand Engineering of Clover‐Shaped Windows in Ligand‐Driven Local Pore‐Space‐Partitioned MOFs for Stepwise Enhancement of Propylene/Ethylene Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT Ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) and propylene (C 3 H 6 ) are core chemical feedstocks, and high‐purity products are critical for downstream polymer production. However, existing adsorbents generally suffer from poor compatibility between pores and target gas molecules. Herein, a ligand‐driven pore space partition strategy was proposed, whereby a cage‐like metal‒organic framework (JLU‐MOF113) was constructed through the self‐assembly of a benzothiadiazole‐functionalized ligand and trinuclear iron cluster. In the framework, the oriented thiadiazole rings on the ligands enable local pore space partition, forming clover‐shaped ultramicroporous windows. Taking JLU‐MOF113 as the parent framework, 1,2,4‐triazole (trz) and tetrazole (taz) were successfully introduced to replace coordinated H 2 O based on terminal ligand engineering. While further blocking the pore windows, the pore environment was optimized, resulting in the preparation of isostructural JLU‐MOF114/115. Through such stepwise regulation, the microenvironment of local pores in MOFs was successfully tailored, enabling a stepwise enhancement in separation selectivity for C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 mixtures. Among them, JLU‐MOF115 exhibits excellent selectivity that surpasses many known MOFs and can separate 73.8 L/kg −1 of C 2 H 4 with a purity of 99.95% from equimolar C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 mixtures. This work enriches MOFs with locally partitioned pore characteristics and provides a novel design strategy for the improvement of gas separation performance in MOFs.

title: Efficient Chirality Transfer Enables Amplified Circularly Polarized Luminescence in Chiral Metal Halides Hybrid Structures
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral organic‐inorganic hybrid metal halides have aroused considerable interest for chiroptical applications. However, developing effective structural design strategies and elucidating the underlying chirality transfer mechanisms remain challenging. Herein, utilizing a structure‐directing strategy, two pairs of enantiomeric hybrid manganese chlorides including one‐dimensional (1D) structures [ R ‐/ S ‐(C 6 H 11 NO 2 ) 3 Mn]·[MnCl 4 ] (denoted as P ‐/ M ‐PCA‐2Mn) and R ‐/ S ‐(C 6 H 11 NO 2 )MnCl 2 (denoted as P ‐/ M ‐PCA‐Mn) were synthesized based on the chiral ligands ( R / S )‐(‐/+)‐piperidine‐3‐carboxylic acid (( R / S )‐(‐/+)‐C 6 H 12 ClNO 2 ). This approach also demonstrates generality and can be extended to systems incorporating different ligands. Magnetic susceptibility measurements revealed that antiferromagnetic spin arrangement may contribute to the 7‐fold emission efficiency enhancement in P ‐PCA‐Mn. Furthermore, the luminescent dissymmetry factor | g lum | value increased from 1.3 × 10 −3 in P ‐PCA‐2Mn to 4.2 × 10 −2 in P ‐PCA‐Mn, which is associated with stronger intramolecular hydrogen‐bonding interactions, more pronounced structural distortion, and an enhanced magnetic transition dipole moment, collectively suggesting their potential contributions to the improved circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) performance. Through integration with liquid crystals, stepwise CPL amplification was achieved, elevating | g lum | to the 10 −1 order of magnitude, which exhibits the enantioselectivity of asymmetric photopolymerization. This work confirms the effectiveness of a structure‐directing strategy in boosting both luminescence efficiency and chirality transfer in chiral hybrid metal halides, and presents a novel and efficient platform for regulating CPL properties.

Hydrogen-based green steel corridors: cost saving and emission reduction potentials of emerging trade routes
abstract: Deploying hydrogen-based direct-reduced iron (H 2 -DRI) technologies will be decisive to defossilize the global steel sector by replacing coal-based blast furnaces (BF) in conventional steelmaking. DRI can then either be directly fed into an electric-arc-furnace (EAF) and alternative electric smelting furnaces or transported as cold hot-briquetted iron (HBI) and a green commoditiy to a steel plant. The availability and expansion of low-cost renewable electricity and green hydrogen supply options is the essential and site-specific precondition to deploy H 2 -DRI plants that can be gradually switched from natural gas to hydrogen. However, near-zero emission steel made from H 2 -DRI needs to produced at competitive costs compared to fossil steel regulated under carbon emission pricing schemes. Based on revised green hydrogen cost forecasts in potentially low-cost countries like Australia or Oman, this study reveals the cost competitiveness of emerging green steel corridors built on international partnerships. With green HBI then exported to a representative EAF green steelmaking site, the analysis shows the potential cost savings of importing green HBI from renewable-rich countries when facing a future lack of affordable hydrogen supply options in leading steel countries like Germany or South Korea characterized by a high dependence on energy imports. Overall, low-emission crude steel based on 66 vol% H 2 -HBI imports achieves fossil cost parity in Germany in 2040 at increased carbon prices in the EU, while all 100% hydrogen-based steel scenarios inhere higher costs with a premium of 6%–13% over natural gas-based DRI-EAF crude steel at 828 € t −1 CS (with 0% scrap) at hydrogen costs ranging between 4.14 and 4.94 € kg −1 H 2 . In addition, a cradle-to-gate accounting of greenhouse gas emissions reveals that cost savings from HBI imports potentially come at the expense of up to 50% higher total emissions compared to an integrated H 2 -DRI-EAF plant running on iron ore pellet imports. All 100% H 2 -DRI-based scenarios yield an emission reduction between 42%–57% compared to a domestic benchmarked NG-DRI-EAF scenario at 1293 kg CO 2 (e) t −1 CS. The carbon footprint analysis further highlights the effect of upstream defossilization measures related to iron ore mining, pelletising and transport by rail and ship.

title: Risk-aware operation of electric vehicle aggregators in uncertain electricity markets using game theory and Markowitz framework
Model-based prediction of temperature evolution in solid-state batteries with minimal experimental data: A case study on composite cathodes under thermal ramp
abstract: While solid-state batteries (SSBs) are presumed to be safer than conventional LIBs, recent studies suggest that they can undergo a quicker and more severe thermal runaway than LIB cells. We have developed a modelling framework to investigate safety of SSBs by linking material-scale measurements to electrode- or cell-scale thermal behaviour. The proposed framework directly incorporates differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) heat flow measurements obtained at a single heating rate as a time-dependent heat source to simulate the temperature evolution of electrodes and cells under prescribed thermal ramp conditions. With minimum experimental data and computational fitting efforts, our model allows for consistent thermal-safety comparisons across cell formats and rapid screening of SSB materials. We implemented our model for cathode composites of SSBs, consisting of LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 and eight different oxide- and sulphide-based solid electrolytes, exposed to a thermal ramp and simulated their temperature evolution. The simulations were run in three representative formats for SSBs: coin, single-layer pouch, and multilayer-pouch cells. The results show that the temperature increase in sulphide-based cathode composites is significantly higher than that of oxide-based composites. Among the different formats, the temperature increases considerably higher in cathode composites with multilayer-pouch format, compared to others. The model was also applied to two 24 Ah LIB cells under a 150 °C oven test, whose temperature evolution results has been reported in the literature. The simulated temperature evolution showed good agreement with the experimental measurements and the corresponding kinetic-based model under the investigated thermal conditions, demonstrating the capability of the simplified approach to translate calorimetric heat generation data into full-cell thermal behaviour and its potential applicability to battery systems with different chemistries.

Surface Texturing Boosts Silicon-Based Tribovoltaic Nanogenerators via Synergistic Edge Electric Field and Tribochemistry
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon-based tribovoltaic nanogenerators (TVNGs) can directly convert sliding-induced interfacial processes into electrical output, but their performance is often limited by inefficient carrier generation and transport. Here, square-pillar arrays were fabricated on monocrystalline silicon to investigate how surface texture affects output magnitude and polarity. Texturing increased the peak current by approximately 25-fold, and both n-type and p-type textured devices exhibited positive current polarity. The p-type device also showed a gradual transition from negative to positive current during initial sliding. Output depended strongly on the longitudinal spacing between pillars and the number of simultaneously engaged transverse rows, whereas no clear monotonic dependence on pillar width was observed under the tested conditions. Among the counterface materials, GCr15 steel produced the highest and most stable output; H62 brass and 1060 aluminum produced lower or unstable currents accompanied by different transfer and oxidation features. Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) revealed a spatially nonuniform surface-potential distribution near pillar edges and a sliding-associated potential change in the trench-bottom region. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) detected SiO2 and substoichiometric silicon oxides on the silicon surface, as well as Fe2O3 in steel-derived wear debris. The strong suppression of output during nitrogen purging further indicates that the response is sensitive to the ambient atmosphere. Taken together, these observations are consistent with a mechanism in which texture-dependent contact and repeated edge encounters modify the interfacial state, while oxide-related transport and oxygen-sensitive tribochemistry contribute to carrier generation and collection. The proposed competition between the built-in electric field (BEF) and an evolving interfacial electric field (IEF) provides a framework for interpreting the polarity transition.

title: Electronic Structure and Charge Separation Modulation of Carbon Nitride by -B(OH)- Groups for Enhanced Photocatalytic Phenol Degradation via Peroxymonosulfate Activation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (CN) has emerged as a promising photocatalyst for peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based advanced oxidation processes, but its performance is constrained by rapid charge recombination and poor PMS activation capability. Herein, we report a boron-doped CN featuring distinctive -B(OH)- groups (OH-BCN20), synthesized via one-step calcination of urea with trace boric acid. The -B(OH)- groups play a pivotal role in PMS activation by strategically modulating the electronic and band structure of CN. Under dark conditions, the electron-deficient B atoms in the -B(OH)- groups serve as primary active sites, facilitating PMS adsorption and subsequent oxidation to generate 1O2. Upon visible light irradiation, photogenerated holes tend to accumulate at B sites, and the resultant efficient charge separation promotes PMS activation. Consequently, the OH-BCN20/PMS/Vis system removes 99.5% of phenol (PE) under visible light, outperforming the CN/PMS/Vis system (38.8%). In the dark, the OH-BCN20/PMS system degrades 43.5% of PE in 60 min, whereas pristine CN shows no activity. This system also demonstrates robust performance in complex water matrices, achieves effective detoxification, and maintains stable continuous-flow operation for 12 h. This study uncovers the critical role of -B(OH)- groups in achieving efficient electronic and band structure modulation of CN, offering a novel paradigm for designing high-performance metal-free catalysts for wastewater treatment.

title: Harnessing Weak Intermolecular Interactions for Efficient PFOA Capture in a Fluorine-Rich Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework Membrane
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D-COF) membranes with open porosity represent a promising class of next-generation materials, particularly for selective molecular separations. In this work, we synthesized a fluorinated 3D-COF membrane (Tam-Tfta) via a liquid–liquid interfacial polymerization reaction for the efficient removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Owing to the abundance of fluorine functional groups within the COF backbone, the membrane achieved quantitative sequestration of PFOA from wastewater at environmentally relevant concentrations (1.0 μg L–1), while maintaining a high water permeance of ∼40 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. Mechanistic analysis reveals that the 3D-COF membrane enables favorable, orientation-assisted interactions within its pores, facilitating effective capture of amphiphilic PFOA molecules in contaminated water. This work represents one of the first demonstrations of a pure 3D COF membrane specifically engineered for removing PFAS.

title: Thickness-Driven Evolution of Third-Order Nonlinear Response in Ternary TMDC MoNbSe2
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thickness variation in 2D materials is essential for nonlinear optical (NLO) applications. Since key nonlinear parameters such as nonlinear absorption, effective nonlinear coefficients, and carrier generation-recovery dynamics change from monolayer to few-layer thicknesses, systematic thickness-dependent measurements are needed to extract reliable NLO parameters and identify optimal regimes for applications including mode-locking, optical switching, and optical limiting. Here, third-order NLO responses of heterometallic ternary transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) MoNbSe2 nanoflakes are observed with varying thicknesses under two excitation wavelengths. Under 1 µm laser excitation, the saturable absorption (SA) behavior diminishes (β decreasing from –42 to –9.7 × 103 cm/GW) with decreasing thickness from approximately 63 to 3 nm, while under 1558 nm excitation, β varies from –10 to –7.6 × 103 cm/GW at low pump intensity and from 11 to 15.2 × 103 cm/GW at high intensities as the thickness is reduced to 3 nm. Notably, at 3 nm thickness under 1 µm excitation, only SA is observed, as the reduced thickness provides a limited carrier population, thereby only a small fraction of photons excites these carriers, while the rest are transmitted. In contrast, at 1.5 µm excitation reverse saturable absorption (RSA) dominates since the incoming lower photon energy promotes absorption through excited-state and defect-state pathways. These results validate wavelength-dependent NLO fundamentals and highlight the versatility of MoNbSe2 for miniaturized photonic technologies. Moreover, the observed SA response is leveraged for ultrafast photonic generation, enabling stable mode-locked pulse formation with a measured pulse duration of 766 fs at 1.5 µm with a repetition rate of 8.011 MHz. Collectively, this study aims to elucidate thickness-dependent NLO mechanisms, and the demonstrated broadband, wavelength-dependent NLO response and mode-locking performance establish MoNbSe2 as a strong candidate for next-generation ultrafast photonic components.

title: Engineering Nitroimidazole-Based Molecular Elements for Hypoxia-Responsive Oligonucleotide Materials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hypoxia-responsive oligonucleotides (ONs) offer a route to conditionally regulate nucleic acid activity in diseased tissues, but the chemical factors that govern their masking and activation remain insufficiently defined. Here, we synthesized four nitroimidazole-modified phosphoramidite monomers derived from adenine (Ah), guanine (Gh), thymine (Th), and cytosine (Ch) and incorporated the Th, Ah, and Gh building blocks into ONs by automated solid-phase synthesis. Using a common parent sequence, we compared Th-, Ah-, and Gh-modified ONs in terms of synthetic compatibility, duplex stability, and reductive release, and further evaluated selected Th-modified ONs in cellular and in vivo studies. Thermal denaturation studies showed that internal Th and Gh modifications caused substantial destabilization of DNA/RNA duplexes, whereas Ah modifications were better tolerated. Under nitroreductase/NADPH reduction conditions, the Gh modification showed the most efficient regeneration of the native ON, while Ah mainly formed reduced but uncleaved products and Th gave partial release. Although Gh provided favorable masking and release behavior, Th offered a more practical balance of synthetic accessibility and duplex inhibition. Th-modified ONs retained Clusterin-silencing activity in MIA PaCa-2 cells and showed hypoxia-associated recovery of activity, and enhanced and prolonged tumor-associated fluorescence in tumor-bearing mice compared with an unmodified control. These results highlight the importance of the tested nucleobase–attachment-site combinations in the design of nitroimidazole-modified ONs.

title: Microneedle-Enabled Metabolic-Redox Amplification Cascade for Suppressing Postoperative Tumor Recurrence
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Residual tumor cells can survive surgical resection by maintaining nutrient supply and antioxidant defenses, thereby driving postsurgical recurrence. Here, we develop a dissolvable microneedle platform, MN-MnO2/MPN, that integrates glucose depletion with redox catalysis to establish a localized metabolic-redox amplification cascade. MnO2 exhibits glucose oxidase-like activity, promoting glucose consumption and H2O2 generation, while the copper-tannic acid metal-polyphenol network facilitates stimulus-responsive Cu2+ release, glutathione depletion, and Fenton-like oxidative catalysis. These coordinated processes amplify intracellular oxidative stress, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction, lipid peroxidation, and tumor cell death. In a 4T1 incomplete-resection model, MN-MnO2/MPN markedly suppresses residual tumor regrowth, reducing tumor weight by approximately 80% and achieving 60% survival at day 38. Mechanistically, treatment decreased intratumoral glucose levels by approximately 60% and increased malondialdehyde levels by 2.5-fold, supporting coordinated metabolic deprivation and oxidative damage in vivo. Transcriptomic analysis further identified 3904 differentially expressed genes, with enrichment of metabolic, oxidative stress, and cell-death-associated pathways. This study shows the potential of locally deployable catalytic therapies that exploit the metabolic and redox vulnerabilities of postoperative residual tumors.

title: Injectable Hydrogels for Programmable Protein Release
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Injectable and degradable hydrogels provide a promising route for controlling the spatiotemporal release of protein therapeutics, yet achieving programmable release kinetics across proteins of different sizes remains challenging. Here, dextran–oxanorbornadiene (OND)/PEG–thiol hydrogels are described that integrate a degradable hydrogel network with tunable Michael addition reactivity to enable hydrolysis-gated and chemically programmable protein release. The OND linkers serve dual functions as crosslinkers forming the hydrogel network and as covalent tethers for protein cargos, allowing kinetic control over tethering efficiency and release rate through the choice of OND variant, precursor mixing sequence, and degree of protein functionalization. Using model proteins of different sizes and structural flexibilities—green fluorescent protein (GFP, 27 kDa), immunoglobulin G (IgG, 150 kDa), and the trimeric ectodomain of the HIV-1 glycoprotein (350 kDa)—the system demonstrates a transition from diffusion-dominated to hydrolysis-gated, non-first-order release behavior. Two mechanistically distinct tethering regimes were identified: reaction-rate-dominated tethering for IgG and competition-limited tethering for GFP, providing complementary routes for controlling cargo retention and release. Additional formulation-level modulation through network density and crosslinker topology provided orthogonal control over release rate and protein loading capacity. Representative cargos subjected to covalent tethering and release preserved protein structure and function after release. Collectively, this study establishes a modular framework for designing injectable OND hydrogels that achieve predictable and customizable release kinetics, offering a versatile platform for long-acting delivery of biologic therapeutics.
