title: A Metabolically Coupled Photochromic Protein AND-Gate for Living Materials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Engineered living materials (ELMs) capable of real-time logical operations would offer transformative opportunities for adaptive sensing and biosecurity. However, conventional synthetic biological logic gates rely heavily on transcriptional regulation, which results in sluggish responses, or depend on exogenous chemical reductants that compromise environmental safety and living autonomy. Here, we report an artificial metabolically coupled photochromic protein, engineered via combined site-specific unnatural amino acid incorporation and cysteine mutagenesis to reconfigure the chromophore microenvironment. At the protein level, this dual engineering is proposed to redirected excited-state energy dissipation from radiative decay toward nonradiative charge transfer, associated with enhancing photoreduction kinetics while enabling living bacteria to produce photochromic responses using intracellular reducing equivalents as “logical fuel”. At the living system level, combining this protein with an intracellular “metabolic clearance” mechanism established a precise “Logic 0” state. By integrating the engineered bacteria into 3D-bioprintable hydrogel matrices, we demonstrated a “metabolic–physical” dual-locking platform, in which encrypted visual data remains hidden under the tested conditions unless simultaneously triggered by specific illumination and metabolic substrate supply. This work links cellular metabolic state with optical responsiveness, offering a approach for designing living materials that combine rapid response with information security.

title: Identification of Potent Target VDAC1 for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Therapy with the Natural Chloroxanthone–Xanthone Heterodimer Molecule Inducing Ferroptosis
abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer‐related mortality, underscoring the need for actionable targets and effective small‐molecule therapeutics. Voltage‐dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), a key regulator of mitochondrial homeostasis, remains incompletely explored as a therapeutic target in HCC. From the endophytic fungus Penicillium sp. RM, we isolated two pairs of enantiomeric heterodimers ( 1 and 2 ) and their monomers ( 3 and 4 ). Penirmxanthone A ( 1 ) is the first reported chloroxanthone‐xanthone heterodimer, whereas penirmxanthone B ( 2 ) features a previously undescribed chloroxanthone‐gentisin scaffold. In vitro, (+)‐ 1 suppressed aggressive phenotypes of HCC cells and induced ferroptosis. Chemical proteomic, biophysical, and genetic analyses identified VDAC1 as a direct and functionally required target of (+)‐ 1 . Mechanistically, (+)‐ 1 engages VDAC1 through K239 and N241, destabilizes the V‐Set and Transmembrane Domain Containing 2 Like (VSTM2L)‐VDAC1‐Hexokinase 2 (HK2) complex, promotes VDAC1 oligomerization, and impairs mitochondrial membrane potential and energy metabolism, culminating in ferroptosis. VDAC1 knockout attenuated these effects, whereas VDAC1 re‐expression restored them. In vivo, VBIT‐4 diminished (+)‐ 1 ‐induced antitumor and ferroptosis‐related effects. Collectively, these findings identify (+)‐ 1 , to our knowledge, as the first natural product that directly targets VDAC1 to promote its oligomerization and induce ferroptosis, highlighting VDAC1 oligomerization as a potential therapeutic target in HCC.

title: Efficient Depolymerization of Polyester Plastic Enabled by Ultrathin Co-Doped ZnO Nanosheets with Abundant Oxygen Vacancies
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The chemical recycling of polyester plastics is a promising sustainable route to resource recycling and environmental protection, yet its success hinges on the development of efficient heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, a high-gravity-assisted strategy using rotating packed bed (RPB) is proposed to continuously and rapidly synthesize ultrathin Co-doped nanosheets (Co/ZnO-RPB) for depolymerizing polyester plastics. Compared to the counterpart of batch-type stirred tank (Co/ZnO-ST), the optimized nanosheets exhibit a 60% reduction in thickness, accompanied by a 2.3-fold enhancement in doping efficiency and a 1.3-fold increase in oxygen vacancy concentration. The as-prepared Co/ZnO-RPB possessed outstanding performance for PLA methanolysis at 105 °C, achieving a methyl lactate (MeLA) formation rate of 521.7 g gcat–1 h–1, which is 1.8 times higher than that of Co/ZnO-ST, exceeding most reported catalysts. Comprehensive characterization and in situ infrared spectroscopy reveal the synergistic mechanism of PLA methanolysis. Oxygen vacancies enhance the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon while driving the cleavage of methanol to generate nucleophilic species, which further drives ester bond cleavage. More importantly, the Co/ZnO-RPB exhibits remarkable versatility by effectively depolymerizing other polyester plastics and various real-life polyester wastes. This work offers a valuable guidance to the challenge of waste polyester plastics accumulation.

title: Self-Assembly–Galvanic Replacement Route to Conformal Ag Nanoflower Interfaces for Dendrite-Suppressed Zn Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rechargeable aqueous Zn anodes are severely limited by sluggish interfacial kinetics and morphological instability. Herein, we report a simple and vacuum-free self-assembly/galvanic replacement strategy that converts a silver nanoplate dispersion into a conformal Ag nanoflower scaffold on Zn foil (Zn@AgNF). This porous and highly wetting metallic interface provides continuous electron-transport pathways and a favorable interfacial environment for Zn nucleation, thereby promoting more uniform Zn deposition and improved interfacial kinetics. Ex situ morphological observations suggest a progressive deposition evolution toward compact Zn deposits with reduced surface oxidation. Symmetric cells exhibit reduced nucleation and growth overpotentials, narrow voltage hysteresis across a wide current-density range, and stable cycling at 10 mA cm–2. In rechargeable Zn–air full cells, Zn@AgNF decreases round-trip polarization and stabilizes interfacial impedance, while improving the full-cell Coulombic efficiency and cycling endurance under the tested conditions (5 mA cm–2 and 1 mAh cm–2). These advantages are maintained in gel electrolytes, in which the cells tolerate repeated bending up to 180°. This work demonstrates a simple solution-based interfacial engineering strategy for improving Zn deposition stability in aqueous Zn-based energy-storage systems.

title: Dynamic Network Engineering of Soy Protein-Based Ionic Hydrogels via Freeze-Locking and Metal Coordination for Intelligent Human–Machine Interaction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The simultaneous achievement of high ionic conductivity and mechanical robustness remains a fundamental challenge for conductive hydrogels, as excessive ionic species often disrupt polymer networks and compromise structural integrity. Herein, a dynamic network engineering strategy integrating PVA freeze-locking, reversible Fe3+ coordination, and ionic conduction is developed to construct a robust ionically conductive hydrogel (IL-PPM0.1-Fe) for intelligent wearable electronics. The freeze-locked PVA crystalline domains establish a rigid physical framework, while reversible Fe3+–MSPI coordination interactions contribute to network reinforcement and energy dissipation. Meanwhile, the incorporation of VBIMBr introduces imidazolium-containing ionic species into the hydrogel system. The resulting hydrogel achieves a tensile strength of approximately 1.5 MPa, a fracture strain of 673%, and an ionic conductivity of 16.2 S/m, while maintaining mechanical integrity over 500 tensile loading–unloading cycles at 100% strain. The sensor exhibits a strain sensing range of 1–500% (GF = 2.14), a pressure sensitivity of 0.21 kPa–1 at 0–1 kPa, and rapid response and recovery times of 230 and 192 ms, respectively. Furthermore, the hydrogel enables human motion monitoring, handwriting recognition, and proof-of-concept Morse-code-based human–machine interaction. This work demonstrates a promising strategy for combining mechanical robustness, ionic conduction, and multifunctional sensing in wearable electronics.

title: Revealing Cu–Mn Electronic Structure in Activated CuMn/Al2O3 Catalyst By Decoupling of Overlapping X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Spectra
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mn-promoted Cu-based catalysts demonstrate high efficiency and stability in various chemical processes, including methanol synthesis. XPS investigations of catalytic reactions and active catalytic centers in Cu–Mn-based catalysts face certain problems: it is challenging to determine the Mn oxidation state because of the strong overlap of Cu and Mn photoelectron and Auger spectra. In this study, a strict background subtraction based on a comprehensive set of standard samples as a reference was applied to separate the net Mn photoelectron spectra from the overlapping Cu signals, which reveals the Mn oxidation state with accurate quantitative analysis. Together with XAS, XRD, and HRTEM evidence, the results jointly support a strong Cu–Mn interaction and changes in their electronic states in the CuMn/Al2O3 catalyst during activation and passivation, providing new insights into the nature of the catalytic centers.

title: Two-Stage Machine Learning-Assisted Multiplex Catecholamine Quantification in Artificial Urine on a Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Paper
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catecholamines, including dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine, are important biomarkers of neurological and neuroendocrine disorders. However, their simultaneous quantification in body fluids remains challenging because of their similar molecular structures, which produce highly overlapping Raman spectroscopic signatures. Here, we develop an integrated platform combining an iron-nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA-Fe)-functionalized surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) paper with a two-stage machine learning pipeline for catecholamine quantification in artificial urine. The SERS paper enables rapid drop-and-measure detection, achieving limits of detection of 7.18, 9.01, and 6.80 μM for dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine in artificial urine, respectively. For samples with unknown compositions, the pipeline first classifies the catecholamines present (92.19% group-level accuracy) and then quantifies single-component samples via intensity-ratio calibration and mixtures via trained partial least squares regression models (global root-mean-square error: 2.27 μM). This work establishes a functionalized SERS paper platform coupled with machine learning as a proof of concept for the identification and quantitative analysis of structurally similar metabolites in complex mixtures.

title: Catalytic Manganese Ferrite Nanoparticles Improve Therapeutic Response in Glioblastoma Spheroids through Hypoxia Mitigation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary brain tumor characterized by treatment resistance, high recurrence rate, and dismal survival, features influenced by tumor hypoxia, a clinically well-established driver of radio- and chemoresistance. Manganese ferrite nanoparticles possess catalase-like activity capable of generating oxygen from tumor-endogenous hydrogen peroxide, offering a strategy to alleviate tumor hypoxia and re-sensitize GBM cells to chemotherapy. In this study, two manganese ferrite compositions (Mn2FeO4 and MnFe2O4) were synthesized using flame spray pyrolysis, characterized, and evaluated for their ability to reduce hypoxia. Nanoparticle internalization and distribution were confirmed in both patient-derived ZH757 and commercial U87MG GBM spheroid models. Both ferrite formulations decreased the hypoxic cell fraction in GBM spheroids after 17 days, without inducing cytotoxicity in normal fibroblasts. Therapeutic in vitro efficacy was assessed on the previously established GliaMimic treatment evaluation platform, which longitudinally monitors tumor progression during a 17-day in vitro treatment regimen of single-fraction radiation (4 Gy) plus multicycle temozolamide (10, 50, 100 μM TMZ) followed by a treatment-free interval. Nanoparticle-treated tumor spheroids exhibited in combination with radio- and chemotherapy enhanced early cytotoxicity and reduced viability and metabolic activity at the end of treatment, compared to the radiation plus TMZ control alone, with treatment benefits generally becoming more pronounced at higher TMZ doses. Notably, after treatment cessation, nanoparticle-treated groups displayed lower post-treatment progression, likely indicating sustained post-treatment efficacy. These findings advance the mechanistic understanding of catalytic nanoparticle-mediated tumor oxygenation, providing a crucial in vitro foundation for its application as an adjuvant strategy to improve therapeutic efficacy in GBM.

title: NIR-Triggered Photothermal-Gated Microneedle Patch for Stage-Responsive Microenvironment Remodeling in Infected Burn Wounds
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving precise and effective treatment of infected burn wounds across different healing stages remains a major challenge in current wound management strategies. To address this issue, we developed a near-infrared (NIR)-responsive photothermal-gated hemin-coated polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/polyacrylamide (PA)/magnesium silicide (Mg2Si) microneedle patch (abbreviated as PPMH), designed to enable spatiotemporally controlled therapeutic gaseous-ionic release for stage-responsive microenvironment remodeling throughout wound healing. The microneedle matrix, constructed from biocompatible polymers, integrates exudate-absorbing components at the base and hydrogen-generating magnesium silicide nanosheets (MN) at the needle tips. A hydrophobic hemin shell serves as a photothermal-responsive gate for on-demand activation. Upon insertion into the wound tissue, the microneedles effectively penetrate biological barriers and establish localized therapeutic interfaces. Upon NIR irradiation, the hemin shell undergoes rapid photothermal conversion, triggering gate opening and controlled hydrogen release within the dermal tissue. During the inflammatory phase, the released hydrogen alleviates oxidative stress and suppresses inflammation, while the photothermal effect of the outer hemin coating exerts potent antibacterial action to clear local bacterial infection. In the subsequent regeneration phase, the sustained release of Mg2+ and Si-containing species promotes angiogenesis and re-epithelialization. Collectively, this system effectively modulates the wound microenvironment in a stage-dependent manner, accelerating tissue regeneration and functional recovery. Therefore, PPMH designed in this study represents a versatile and translational platform for stage-responsive microenvironment remodeling and multi-targeted treatment of complex burn wounds.

title: Printable Fe-Containing Apatitic Cement Scaffolds Coupling Sustained Platelet Lysate Release and Osteogenic Stimulation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Printable apatitic calcium phosphate cement (CPC) scaffolds integrating bioceramic particles, growth factors, and a polymer-based matrix were developed as an innovative strategy toward biomimetic bone substitutes. Iron-doped calcium phosphate (FeCaP) microparticles and human platelet lysates (PLs) were incorporated into a natural polymer-based matrix to create CPC-based inks that can be processed by Direct Ink Writing. CPC-based scaffolds containing FeCaP (Fe-CPC) and Fe-CPC/PL with controlled architecture, high shape fidelity, defined macroporosity, and compressive strength in the trabecular bone range (10–15 MPa) were successfully printed. After 21 days of immersion at 37 °C, the scaffolds preserved structural integrity, exhibited moderate degradation (5.77–6.23% mass loss), and sustained the release of PL-derived proteins of up to 82%, while the magnetic response of the FeCaP phase was preserved. In vitro, Fe-CPC/PL scaffolds supported human adipose-derived stem cell (hASC) attachment, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation. Higher early bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) secretion was followed by higher osteopontin (OPN) and osteocalcin (OCN) expression at later stages (∼9- and ∼3-fold, respectively, vs CPC), consistent with an osteogenic-supportive microenvironment. These findings demonstrate that Fe-CPC/PL is a 3D-printable apatitic scaffold that combines structural support with sustained biological signaling, with strong potential as a next-generation hybrid composite bone substitute.

title: The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: 2D Perovskite Seed-Mediated Crystallization Regulation for Stable and High-Performance Carbon-Based Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract During low-temperature solution processing, the rapid crystallization of three-dimensional (3D) perovskites often lead to disordered nucleation and severe defects at surfaces and grain boundaries. Introducing 2D perovskite seeds into the precursor is an effective strategy for modulating the crystallization of 3D perovskites. However, the effects of 2D seeds on the chemical stability of perovskite precursors, as well as the mechanisms by which they regulate perovskite nucleation and crystal growth, remain unclear. Herein, 2D perovskite crystals (DFPD)2PbI4 are synthesized through a slow-cooling crystallization method and employed as seeds to regulate 3D perovskite crystallization. The results reveal that the regulatory effects of the 2D seeds extend across multiple stages of perovskite formation and establish a more favorable crystallization pathway. The 2D seeds facilitate nucleation by lowering the associated Gibbs free energy barrier while moderating subsequent crystal growth, thereby promoting the formation of larger grains and smoother perovskite films. The residual 2D phase interacts with the Pb–I framework through N–H⋯I hydrogen bonding and coordination with uncoordinated Pb2+, further passivating defects and establishing a favorable band alignment with the 3D perovskite. Consequently, the incorporation of 2D seeds enables carbon-based perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs) to achieve a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 17.39%, outperforming the control device. In addition, the presence of 2D seeds effectively suppresses colloidal aggregation and retards the formation of I3– species during precursor aging, contributing to improved precursor stability. The target C-PSCs without encapsulation maintain 90% of their original PCE after 40 days in ambient conditions, reflecting an enhanced operational long-term stability. This work reveals how the low-dimensional (LD) perovskite seed affects the 3D perovskite crystallization and offers a promising strategy for improved PCE and stable C-PSCs.

title: Light-Programmable Broad-Spectrum CPC-like Surfactants as Environmentally Benign Alternatives to Cationic Antimicrobial Agents
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs), particularly cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC), are widely employed as antimicrobial agents in personal care, hygiene, and pharmaceutical applications. However, the extensive and sustained use of CPC and related QACs has accelerated the emergence of microbial resistance, a consequence attributable in part to their exceptional chemical stability. In this work, we report a new class of photoactive CPC-like platforms (2a–l) featuring diverse structural motifs, including a sulfide linkage, that confer superior antimicrobial performance relative to legacy QACs. The most effective CPC-like surfactants (2b and 2k) exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including Streptococcus mutans, Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of approximately 1–8 μg/mL. Furthermore, these surfactants generate type II reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon photochemical activation, supplementing the type I ROS produced by the pyridinium moiety. The critical micellar concentration (CMC) of these surfactants was, on average, one order of magnitude lower than that of CPC, an enhancement attributed to the presence of the sulfide motifs. Importantly, these sulfide moieties can be released as aroma or bioactive fragments upon induced photochemical degradation, providing a built-in mechanism for environmental remediation. This work offers a sustainable and multifunctional alternative to legacy QACs, effectively addressing their principal shortcomings of environmental persistence and ecological toxicity.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: d 5 ‐Probed Interlocked Charge‐Structural Disorder Enables Deep Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ Redox Chemistry in Layered Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Mn‐based layered oxide cathodes are attractive for next‐generation rechargeable batteries, owing to their abundant resources and rich redox chemistry, but achieving reversible deep Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ redox remains challenging. Herein, we developed an interlocked charge‐structural disorder protocol in P2‐derived Na 0.67 Fe 0.1 Mn 0.9 O 2 to regulate Mn redox and stabilize discharge voltage. A disordered cation framework is engineered through electronic configuration and atomic rearrangement, where Fe 3+ (d 5 , half‐filled) breaks charge periodicity, and rapid quenching prevents structural reordering to eliminate Fe/Mn order. Electron energy‐loss spectroscopy (EELS) reveals suppressed Mn 4+ /Mn 3+ charge ordering, which enables extended Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ redox as confirmed by soft x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (sXAS). The optimized cathode quenched at 700°C nearly doubles the Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ redox contribution within the Mg‐compatible window (1.8–1.6 V vs. Mg 2+ /Mg) from 15.2% to 29.4%, and it delivers 291.3 Wh kg −1 energy density (based on the mass of active cathode) with capacity retention increased from 62.4% to 87.5% over 50 cycles. Mechanistically, the interlocked disorder lowers the migration barrier by flattening the electrostatic‐potential landscape and enhances the thermodynamic driving force for Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ by destabilizing Jahn–Teller correlations. This work establishes charge‐state disorder as a versatile design principle for layered oxide cathodes, enabling deep, reversible transition‐metal redox for advanced energy storage.

title: Temporal Fidelity Reveals Transient Dissolution Chemistry at Dynamic Electrocatalyst Interfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic electrocatalyst dissolution consists of short‐lived, potential‐dependent interfacial events tied to surface redox, reconstruction, and catalysis. Accurate interpretation of these processes requires preserving the temporal link between metal release and electrochemical state, but this link is often lost in electrochemical inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (EC‐ICP‐MS) due to transport‐induced signal convolution. Here we reduce this distortion by using thin‐layer hydrodynamic confinement to improve near‐electrode convective removal. Paired‐pulse dissolution experiments show that two consecutive 2 s dissolution inputs separated by 50 ms remain distinguishable. Cu‐pulse residence‐time‐distribution measurements and computational fluid dynamics further identify electrode‐region convective coverage and near‐electrode flow velocity as key determinants of signal broadening. Applying this temporal fidelity to representative noble‐metal, carbide, nitride, hydroxide, oxide, and single‐atom interfaces under fast cyclic voltammetry reveals distinct dynamic dissolution fingerprints. This approach further resolves weak reoxidation‐associated Ir dissolution from reduced IrO x and oxygen‐reduction‐associated suppression of spontaneous Cu release from Cu–N–C. These results highlight the importance of temporal fidelity for assigning transient dissolution chemistry at dynamic electrocatalyst interfaces.

title: Conformational Locking in Covalent Organic Frameworks Promotes Coupled H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis and Organic Valorization
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer a compelling platform for coupling photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production with organic valorization. However, the practical efficiency remains limited by rapid electron‐hole recombination. Inspired by the conformational rigidity and planar geometry imposed by peptide bonds, we develop a conformational locking strategy that introduces a fused‐ring linker, which restricts backbone rotation and thereby enhances framework planarity and conjugation, affording a series of COFs (TFPPy‐DATMBP, TFPPy‐DABP, and TFPPy‐DAPy) with progressively improved planarity and conjugation. The conformationally locked TFPPy‐DAPy achieves an impressive H 2 O 2 production rate of 119.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , with an apparent quantum yield up to 29.14% at 410 nm, while delivering a yield of >98% toward the high‐value imine product. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the conformationally locked TFPPy‐DAPy extends the lifetime of the long‐lived charge‐separated state by approximately 10‐fold to 102.87 ps, compared with 10.34 ps for TFPPy‐DATMBP. This work establishes TFPPy‐DAPy as an efficient photocatalyst for fine chemical co‐production, and provides a generalizable molecular‐level design strategy for developing advanced catalysts across diverse photocatalytic applications.

title: Band‐Filling Engineering in Covalent Organic Frameworks Through Host–Guest Charge‐Transfer Interactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Band‐filling engineering is one of the most rational approaches to controlling the electronic properties of inorganic solids such as cuprates, in which electron/hole doping using heterovalent substitution leads to a rigid‐band shift of the Fermi level. In organic solids, a significant obstacle to accurately predicting electronic properties is the difficulty in maintaining the packing structure during molecular substitution. Here, we utilized a covalent organic framework (COF) in which π‐conjugated electron‐donating molecules are covalently linked to form one‐dimensional pore channels. The introduction of a well‐defined amount of electron‐accepting molecules without disrupting the framework structure enabled the first successful demonstration of the deliberate band‐filling control while elucidating the charge state through various spectroscopic measurements. Enhanced electronic itinerancy facilitated by host–guest charge transfer was evidenced by spectroscopic, transport, and magnetic measurements in support of theoretical calculations. The present study opens a new avenue for exploring more advanced electronic organic solids based on band‐filling engineering.

title: Photothermal Upcycling of Waste Polyolefins to Ethylene and Propylene Over Waste Plastic‐Derived Carbon Catalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficient valorization of polyolefin wastes is challenged by the inertness of C─C bonds and the poor selectivity for olefins, which severely limits the conversion efficiency under mild conditions. Herein, a “treating waste with waste” strategy is proposed by using polypropylene waste derived carbon nanospheres (PP‐C) as the photothermal catalyst for polyethylene (PE) upgrading under focused Xenon light irradiation. Comprehensive characterizations identify that sp 2 ‐C domains with abundant edge defects of PP‐C serve as the catalytic active sites, which enable outstanding photothermal conversion and facilitate photogenerated charge separation. Theoretical calculations reveal that zigzag edges of sp 2 ‐structured graphene suppress the recombination of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby the localized electrons at the edge sites effectively weakens C─C bonds on the absorbed reactant and improves the photothermal catalytic efficiency. A remarkable olefin yield of ~60% with approximately 100% PE conversion is achieved within 10 min using PP‐C catalyst under sunlight condition, demonstrating great potential for practical applications. This work not only establishes a sustainable route for plastic valorization but also actively advances an innovative concept for the focused‐sunlight‐drives upgrading of polyolefins.

title: Mechanism of Zwitterionic Photochromism in Aza‐Diarylethenes Revealed by Direct Observation of a Closed‐Ring Intermediate
abstract: ABSTRACT Aza‐diarylethenes represent a unique class of photochromic molecules with reaction pathways inaccessible to conventional diarylethenes. Some aza‐diarylethenes form zwitterionic closed‐ring photoproducts, but direct experimental evidence for the elementary processes remains lacking. Here, we investigate the photochromic mechanism of a benzofuran‐fused aza‐diarylethene ( BF‐ADE ) using steady‐state spectroscopy, transient absorption spectroscopy, time‐resolved infrared spectroscopy, oxygen‐quenching experiments, single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction, and density functional theory calculations. These complementary studies demonstrate that photoirradiation ultimately affords the zwitterionic closed‐ring isomer BF‐ADE(c‐ Z ) , whereas thermal bleaching proceeds via the neutral closed‐ring isomer BF‐ADE(c) . Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy revealed a 1.6 ps process, and time‐resolved infrared spectroscopy provided direct evidence for the formation of the conventional closed‐ring intermediate BF‐ADE(c) within the first few picoseconds after photoexcitation. Oxygen‐quenching experiments and DFT calculations further showed that BF‐ADE(c‐ Z ) is generated predominantly from BF‐ADE(c) on the ground‐state potential energy surface rather than through a triplet‐mediated pathway. These results provide the first experimental validation of the proposed mechanism of zwitterionic photochromism in aza‐diarylethenes.

title: Three-Dimensional COF/rGO/AuNP Porous Membranes for Enrichment-Enhanced Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering Detection of Aldehydes in Exhaled Breath
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, highlighting the need for noninvasive approaches for early disease screening. Volatile aldehydes in exhaled breath have emerged as promising biomarkers because their concentrations may reflect disease-associated metabolic changes; however, their low abundance and inefficient interaction with SERS substrates remain challenging for reliable breath analysis. Herein, a three-dimensional porous membrane composed of covalent organic framework/reduced graphene oxide/gold nanoparticles (COF/rGO/AuNP) was developed as a SERS substrate for sensitive detection of volatile aldehydes in exhaled breath. The membrane was functionalized with 4-aminothiophenol (4-ATP) for selective aldehyde capture through Schiff-base formation. The combination of COF-mediated gas enrichment and electromagnetic enhancement from AuNPs enabled ultrasensitive aldehyde detection, with a detection limit of 0.28 ppb for benzaldehyde. The platform exhibited excellent selectivity, signal uniformity, reproducibility, and resistance to humidity interference. Its practical applicability was demonstrated by analyzing exhaled breath samples from healthy volunteers and patients with lung cancer, revealing distinct differences in aldehyde concentration profiles between the two groups. This work provides a simple and sensitive membrane-based SERS platform for trace gaseous aldehyde analysis and demonstrates its potential for noninvasive breath-based lung cancer screening.

title: Ultrasound-Based Physiological Sensing: Challenges, Strategies, and Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ultrasound is well suited to repeated deep-tissue imaging, but it rarely measures local biochemical conditions directly. Stimuli-responsive chemistry enables materials to respond to physiological cues through physicochemical changes, yet these changes are not necessarily detectable by ultrasound. Multiscale structural organization can bridge this gap by translating and amplifying molecular or nanoscale responses into larger-scale material changes that produce detectable acoustic signals. The field is progressing from proof-of-concept demonstrations of material responses towards integrated sensing platforms. Advances across these platforms include bioresorption, multiparametric sensing, and repeated measurements over defined periods in animal models. This review examines how responsive chemistry and multiscale structural design jointly enable ultrasound-readable physiological sensing. It also considers the requirements for reliable operation in vivo. Looking ahead, integration with wearable and conformal ultrasound interfaces, soft robotic systems, and AI-assisted decoding could enable longitudinal, personalized, and multiparametric sensing across internal organs and tissue interfaces.

title: Fe3+ Post-Coordination-Locked Polyaryl Ether-Based Aerogels for Solar-Driven Interfacial Evaporation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Water-processable polymers are ideal materials for solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE) due to their advantages in homogeneous processing and oriented molding. However, their inherently high hydrophilicity makes them highly susceptible to swelling or dissolution during operation. Here, we resolve the trade-off between processability and stability by employing a post-coordination locking strategy with Fe3+ in sulfonated poly(phthalazinone ether sulfone ketone) (SPPESK)-based aerogels. Polydopamine-coated molybdenum disulfide (PDA@MoS2) was introduced as a photothermal component, and vertically aligned water-conducting channels were constructed using directional freezing technology. Fe3+ was subsequently introduced to stabilize the prefabricated scaffold. The resulting aerogel maintained its structural integrity even after 192 h of immersion in water. The surface temperature of the aerogel reached 75 °C, with an evaporation rate of 2.4 kg m–2 h–1 and an energy utilization efficiency of 97.3% under one-sun irradiance. Its evaporation performance remained stable even after repeated cycling tests, and the evaporation flux could still reach 1.1 kg m–2 h–1 even under overcast conditions. This ‘build-then-lock’ strategy provides a viable solution for polyaryl ether-based, striking a balance between water treatment performance and operational stability.

title: Rational Donor–Acceptor Design of Dye-Doped Conjugated Polymer Nanoparticles for Ratiometric Oxygen Sensing: Toward Hydrogel Platforms for Corneal Hypoxia Monitoring
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Corneal hypoxia, often induced by contact lens wear, is a precursor to severe ophthalmological pathologies. Early detection requires sensitive, noninvasive oxygen monitoring tools. We present a ratiometric optical oxygen sensor based on conjugated polymer nanoparticles (NP) of poly(fluorene-alt-benzothiadiazole) (F8BT) doped with platinum tetrabenzoporphyrin (BPPt). Spectral overlap between F8BT emission and BPPt absorption promotes efficient energy transfer to the porphyrin. Intersystem crossing then populates its triplet state (3BPPt*), whose phosphorescence is quenched by O2, whereas F8BT fluorescence is O2-insensitive and serves as the internal reference. The first design criterion concerns the choice of dopant: BPPt was selected because 3BPPt* lies energetically below 3F8BT* thereby limiting reverse triplet energy transfer and preserving BPPt phosphorescence. Monte Carlo simulations, constrained by two independent sets of experimental data, indicate that BPPt can deactivate the polymer by a second route that does not populate 3BPPt*. This led to a second design criterion: the doping level must be optimized for balanced dual emission, not for maximum energy transfer. The overall design yields a robust ratiometric sensor in aqueous suspension, with an estimated detection limit of 0.002 mM O2 and a reversible response over repeated O2/N2 cycling. Response times are practical (t90 < 20 s in hydrogel) and likely limited by mass transport. These sensor NP were incorporated into a poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate) (pHEMA) model hydrogel relevant to contact-lens materials. The hydrogel-sensor composite retained ratiometric oxygen-sensing capability and the model matrix remained transparent and swellable; preliminary non-ocular cell assays showed no detectable acute cytotoxicity under the conditions tested. These results establish proof of concept for preserving the sensor function after immobilization in a hydrated pHEMA matrix relevant to future corneal-oxygen-sensing studies.

title: Triple-Robust p -Aramid Copolymer Fibers via Comonomer Engineering: Concurrent Mechanical, Thermal, and Chemical Durability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Para-aramid (p-aramid) fibers have long been the benchmark for ballistic and structural protection owing to their outstanding tensile strength and energy-absorption capability. However, conventional aramid fibers have been predominantly optimized for mechanical loading, limiting their reliability under high-temperature and chemically aggressive environments typical of modern multi-threat defense applications. Addressing this limitation requires a molecular design strategy that balances mechanical performance with thermal and chemical durability. Herein, we report triple-robust p-aramid copolymer (p-AC) fibers engineered through comonomer engineering. 2,7′-Diaminofluorene (2,7′-DAF) was incorporated as a functional comonomer into a 3,4′-oxydianiline-based p-aramid backbone, where its rigid and planar molecular geometry promoted molecular orientation, crystallinity, and chain packing within the copolymer framework. The p-AC fibers maintain high tensile strengths of 2.8–3.3 GPa while achieving a tensile modulus of up to 98.3 GPa. Beyond mechanical performance, the fibers exhibit enhanced thermal and chemical durability, with tensile strength retention reaching up to 86% after thermal aging at 300 °C for 6 h and 70% after exposure to 60 wt % nitric acid for 6 h, surpassing those of commercial benchmark aramid fibers. This study establishes comonomer engineering as a scalable molecular design pathway for next-generation p-aramid fibers capable of reliable operation under coupled mechanical, thermal, and chemical stresses in multi-threat defense environments.

title: Bacterial Extract with Immunomodulatory Properties Ameliorates DSS-Induced Colitis Partly by Inhibiting Ferroptosis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ulcerative colitis (UC) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disorder that affects the digestive tract. OM-85, a bacterial extract known for its immunomodulatory properties, has been investigated in this study for its potential therapeutic effects on dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis. The study comprehensively evaluated inflammatory markers, mucosal integrity, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in colonic tissues. Additionally, the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins was analyzed using Western blotting, while immune cell populations were assessed through multiplexed immunohistochemistry. Oral administration of OM-85 significantly alleviated colitis symptoms in DSS-treated mice by reducing inflammation and tissue damage and by enhancing mucosal barrier integrity. Moreover, OM-85 treatment reduced ROS levels, suppressed the ferroptosis pathway, and restored the Th17/Treg balance in DSS-induced colitis. OM-85 treatment could partly ameliorate DSS-induced gut dysbiosis and regulate various metabolic pathways, including Th17 cell differentiation. By inhibiting the ferroptosis pathway in vitro, OM-85 could alleviate inflammation in LPS-stimulated NCM-460 cells. The results revealed that OM-85 administration could relieve colitis-associated symptoms through downregulating the ferroptosis pathway, which may provide a potential therapeutic option for UC.

title: Solvent-Specific Surface Reconstruction Enables Robust CsPbBr3 Perovskite Heterostructures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Inorganic perovskites boast exceptional thermal and environmental stability, rendering them attractive for transparent photovoltaics and tandem cells. However, conventional post-treatment approaches fail to generate low-dimensional surface layers capable of defect passivation on all-inorganic perovskite films. The fundamental mechanisms behind this limitation remain unclear, and reliable fabrication protocol to fabricate 2D/3D perovskite heterostructures remain largely underexplored. Herein, we develop a solvent-selective surface reconstruction strategy to construct 2D/3D CsPbBr3 perovskite heterostructures. This strategy incorporates trace coordinating solvents into passivation formulations in order to establish coordination interactions with undercoordinated surface lead sites, tune the surface chemical environment of CsPbBr3, and facilitate the spontaneous generation of the n = 1 Ruddlesden–Popper phase. With this strategy implemented, thermally evaporated CsPbBr3 perovskite films exhibit suppressed interfacial charge carrier recombination and optimized interfacial quality. The corresponding solar cells reach a power conversion efficiency of 9.927% and a remarkable open-circuit voltage of 1.654 V, ranking among the highest reported performance for evaporated CsPbBr3. More encouragingly, the resultant devices demonstrate outstanding stability under shelf storage and thermal aging conditions. This work opens a new pathway to fabricate 2D/3D heterostructures for all-inorganic perovskites.

title: Antimetastatic Sulfonate-Functionalized Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Enhance Irinotecan Stability and Delivery for Colorectal Cancer Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with irinotecan (IRI) serving as a backbone chemotherapeutic despite its dose-limiting toxicities, instability of the active lactone form, and lack of intrinsic antimetastatic activity. To overcome these barriers, we developed sulfonate-functionalized mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs), referred to as (SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA, as a multifunctional nanocarrier for IRI delivery. This nanoformulation markedly enhanced drug loading efficiency and preserved over 90% of IRI in its lactone form for up to six months, enabling sustained release and improved pharmacological stability. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient nanoparticle internalization, while IRI@(SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA enhanced apoptosis and reduced the IC50 compared with free IRI. Beyond drug delivery, (SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA exhibited intrinsic antimetastatic activity associated with modulation of focal adhesion kinase/paxillin signaling and impaired tumor cell adhesion and migration. The nanoparticles also exhibited efficient tumor accumulation through the enhanced permeability and retention effect. Pharmacokinetic analysis further revealed that IRI@(SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA prolonged systemic retention, maintaining approximately threefold higher IRI plasma concentrations than free IRI. IRI@(SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA significantly inhibited both primary tumor growth and metastatic dissemination in orthotopic and heterotopic colorectal cancer models, while markedly reducing systemic toxicities and preserving bone marrow cellularity relative to free IRI and liposomal IRI (Onivyde). Transcriptomic profiling further revealed attenuation of extracellular matrix/mesenchymal remodeling and hypoxia/vascular-associated programs, providing molecular support for the observed antimetastatic phenotype. Consistently, reduced vascular endothelial growth factor expression and tumor-associated angiogenesis were observed in the chorioallantoic membrane model. Tumor immune-cell profiling was also performed to assess potential changes in major tumor-associated immune-cell populations. This dual-functional nanomedicine therefore provides an innovative therapeutic strategy that not only augments IRI efficacy but also confers metastasis suppression and favorable pharmacokinetics, addressing critical unmet needs in mCRC treatment. These findings highlight the translational potential of IRI@(SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA as a safer and more effective therapeutic strategy for mCRC.

title: Anion-Immobilizing Poly(ionic liquid) Copolymer Electrolytes for Flame-Retardant Lithium Metal Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer electrolytes have emerged as promising alternatives for next-generation (quasi-) solid-state lithium metal batteries (LMBs), owing to their intrinsic safety, mechanical flexibility, and good processability. Nevertheless, their practical application is severely impeded by low room-temperature ionic conductivity and insufficient Li+ transport arising from sluggish polymer segmental dynamics. Herein, we design a thin (∼57 μm) poly(ionic liquid)-based copolymer electrolyte (CPIL) via copolymerization of 1-vinyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide and methyl methacrylate, which is integrated with a PVDF-HFP matrix and EMIMTFSI plasticizer. The incorporation of poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) endows the electrolyte with high flame retardancy, excellent thermal stability, and superior ionic conductivity (0.524 mS cm–1). Benefiting from the anion anchoring units of PIL, the Li+ transference number is significantly increased to 0.65, thereby enhancing Li+ transport efficiency and inducing even Li deposition on the anode surface. Consequently, the Li|CPIL-2|Li batteries display stable plating/stripping over 2000 h with low polarization of ∼75 mV at 0.1 mA cm–2. The Li|LiFePO4 batteries with CPIL-2 exhibit high-rate performance and long-term cycling stability, with a capacity retention of 65.3% at 0.5 C after 400 cycles. Beyond these, Li|CPIL-2|LiFePO4 pouch cells continue to light LEDs even after cutting and folding, highlighting the potential applications of CPIL for high-energy-density and safety LMBs.

title: Chemoselective Electrochemical Ring Cleavage of Naphthols Enabling Structural Diversification
abstract: ABSTRACT Structural modification of aromatic frameworks by breaking core C─C bonds is challenging due to their inherent stability. Herein, we introduce an electrochemical dearomative ring‐cleavage method that converts readily available β ‐naphthols into synthetically versatile, stereodefined ring‐opened esters with broad functional‐group tolerance. Further ring reconstructions provided various carbocycles and heterocycles, highlighting the synthetic versatility of this strategy for the skeletal modification of aromatic frameworks. Mechanistic studies, including intermediate isolation, cyclic voltammetry, and electrode surface analysis, support a stepwise multielectron oxidation process. In this approach, controlled anodic oxidation, cathodically generated nucleophiles, and proton‐coupled electron transfer collectively govern chemo‐ and stereoretentive C─C bond cleavage.

title: Differentiable Solvation Shell Model for Rational Electrolyte Design
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tailoring the Li+ solvation shell is a central design principle for many emerging Li metal battery electrolytes but remains largely qualitative. Here, we introduce a mean-field Ising model that predicts the Li+ solvation shell from the donor number (DN), acceptor number, molar ratio, and molecular size. The model is end-to-end differentiable, enabling direct parameterization from molecular dynamics (MD) solvation structures. For localized high-concentration electrolytes, it reproduces MD shell compositions with 10.7% RMSE at much reduced cost and captures solvation trends in other electrolyte classes without re-fitting. Model interaction terms show that DN dominates Li+ solvation energetics, explaining the empirical DN-based design rules. For LiTFSI in tetraglyme absent from training, the model identifies fluorobenzene as a diluent and a concentration window with anion-rich solvation shells and low free solvent. The predicted solvation structure is confirmed by MD, and published experiments on related electrolytes support the design principles.

title: A spectral-spatial interweaver for hyperdimensional photonic computing
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Photonic computing offers high bandwidth, parallelism and energy efficiency for artificial intelligence (AI), yet its scalability remains limited by bulky optical components and immature optoelectronic integration. Here we present HyperON, a thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) hyperdimensional optical network built around a passive spectral-spatial interweaver and broadband wavelength-parallel modulators. The interweaver combines wavelength multiplexing with spatial replication in a log2P-stage network, delivering the full wavelength set to every spatial output without beam-combination loss. By interweaving P spectral channels with K spatial units, HyperON forms a unified P × K parallel computing framework, supporting O(N2) operations with only O(N) modulators, improving hardware efficiency and scalability. A 16 × 16 interweaver shows low-loss, broadband and highly uniform operation across 1523.40-1568.85 nm, with 1.30 dB average loss, 0.196 dB output-port variation and 0.414 dB cross-wavelength variation. The integrated wavelength-parallel modulators retain system-level bandwidths of 53-67 GHz after large-scale routing, while standalone devices exhibit bandwidths beyond 67 GHz. Together, these features enable the fabricated HyperON chip to deliver a projected peak throughput of 32.8 TMAC/s, with estimated energy and area efficiencies of 7.04 TMAC/s/W and 0.163 TMAC/s/mm2, respectively. Experimental demonstrations in image convolution, handwritten digit recognition, and 64-mode parallel computing confirm its high speed operation, versatility, and scalability for large-scale AI workloads.

title: De novo identification of protein domains in cryo-electron tomography maps from AlphaFold2 models
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sub-tomogram averaging of cryo-electron tomography maps often fails to reach the resolution required for atomic model building based on side-chain information, preventing accurate protein identification from the density alone. We develop DomainSeeker, which identifies protein domains by integrating AlphaFold2 models with experimental data. It partitions these models into domains by clique analysis of predicted aligned errors, fits them into segmented densities, and evaluates each fit globally and locally, deriving prior probabilities. Bayesian inference integrates the priors with cross-linking mass spectrometry, computing posterior probabilities. Applying prior probability analysis to mouse sperm microtubule doublet densities reveals higher recognition accuracy and resolution robustness than existing approaches. Incorporating cross-linking mass spectrometry for yeast nuclear pore complex densities further improves recognition performance and confidence. An interactive ChimeraX plugin facilitates user access. In this work, DomainSeeker addresses a bottleneck in in situ structural biology and supports visual proteomics in native cellular environments.

title: Sulfur Substitution of Oxygen‐Induced Multiferroic Phase Transition in Chiral Supramolecular Crystals
abstract: ABSTRACT Multiferroics exhibiting multiple ferroic orders have gained tremendous attention for decades owing to their intriguing properties and potential applications in future multifunctional devices. However, despite their unique advantages, such as inherent chirality—in contrast to traditional inorganic multiferroics, the design of molecular multiferroics with ferroelectricity and ferroelasticity remains a great challenge. Herein, through oxygen–sulfur (O/S) heavier congener substitution, we successfully designed the first chiral supramolecular ferroelectric–ferroelastic multiferroics [( R / S )‐1‐(2‐fluorophenyl)ethylamounium)(1‐thia‐15‐crown‐5)]BF 4 . We found that O/S substitution on parent chiral supramolecular compounds with no phase transition results in a 222F2‐type ferroelectric/ferroelastic multiferroic phase transition at 350 K, which can be attributed to the fact that the lower electronegativity of S than O weakens intermolecular interactions in the supramolecular system to reduce the energy barrier for molecular motions. Moreover, the O/S substitution induces remarkable chiral amplification, with the dissymmetry factor of the second‐harmonic generation circular dichroism (SHG‐CD) response one order of magnitude larger than that of the parent counterpart. Notably, such an SHG‐CD response can be switched from a high to a low state during the multiferroic phase transition. Our work opens up a new avenue for constructing multiferroic phase transitions in molecular systems and sheds light on the further exploration of chiral supramolecular multiferroics.

title: Dipole‐Polarized Tri‐Pore COF Delivers Electrons to an O 2 ‐Enriched Pore for H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Although covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ordered and tunable, the structural homogeneity of conventional COFs leaves charge delivery and O 2 activation spatially and functionally uncoupled, limiting both H 2 O 2 selectivity and yield. Here, we report a three‐component, tri‐pore COF by integrating para‐phenylenediamine into a binary fluorenone‐pyrene framework. The asymmetric tri‐pore architecture selectively channels O 2 into one pore before reduction, while the built‐in dipole polarization field‌ directs electrons to the O 2 ‐occupied pore. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy shows excited‐state carrier lifetime is doubled, thereby enabling exclusive electron delivery to that O 2 ‐preconcentrated pore. Molecular dynamics simulations and in situ infrared spectroscopy further reveal favorable O 2 adsorption behavior and an *OOH‐mediated pathway. The COF exhibits a photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production rate of 6.04 mmol g − 1 h − 1 in pure water under O 2 , surpassing its two single‐pore counterparts by respective factors of 18.9 and 6.4. An 18.9‐fold increase in the reaction rate, far exceeding the 3.0‐fold enhancement in the electric field, is not another routine charge‐separation effect but a pore‐specific charge‐delivery effect: electrons are shuttled to the pore where O 2 has already been adsorbed, and *OOH is formed predominantly at that O 2 ‐enriched pore. For next‐generation COF photocatalysts, delivering O 2 mass transport to the catalytic pore should be prioritized over simply enhancing the electric field.

title: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ocean-based geochemical CO2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO2 from the atmosphere. Their viability at scale depends on efficiency. Here, we develop a unified framework for evaluating the efficiencies of ocean geochemical perturbations: OAE adds alkalinity, DOR removes dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and combined alkalinity and DIC addition (ADA) adds both simultaneously. Using a global ocean biogeochemical model, we map global and seasonal DOR efficiency and compare it with OAE efficiency. Further, we show that OAE and DOR simulations can be combined to quantify the effect of simultaneous perturbations in alkalinity and DIC. This enables direct quantification of the oceanic fate of ADA perturbations from approaches such as enhanced rock weathering, riverine alkalinity enhancement and accelerated weathering of limestone. In these approaches, the added alkalinity partially equilibrates with CO2 before entering the ocean, effectively adding both alkalinity and DIC.

title: EcoVAE: a generative deep learning method for global species distribution prediction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anthropogenic pressures on biodiversity necessitate efficient and scalable methods to predict global species distributions. Current species distribution models (SDMs) face challenges with large-scale datasets, complex species associations, and data quality. Here, we introduce EcoVAE, an autoencoder-based generative model that integrates bioclimatic variables with georeferenced occurrences. The model is trained separately for plants, butterflies, and mammals to predict global distributions at both genus and species levels. Through unsupervised learning, EcoVAE captures underlying distribution patterns from large-scale species occurrence data. It achieves high precision and speed, outperforming traditional SDMs in spatial block cross-validation. EcoVAE also reveals signatures of species associations that align with known prey-predator relationships. Taken together, these capacities enable the robust evaluation of global sampling efforts and interpolates distributions in data-limited regions, offering new applications for biodiversity exploration and monitoring.

title: Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Global glacier recession is driving a rapid increase in the number and volume of ice-marginal lakes, leading to more frequent Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The long-term impact of GLOFs on glacier dynamics remains poorly understood, including in Greenland, which holds the largest glacial lake volume in the world. Here, using multi-decadal observations from Isortuarsuup Sermia, Southwest Greenland, we reveal that cyclical GLOFs regulate ice sheet motion. We identify a ‘sawtooth’ pattern of ice-dynamics, whereby multi-year acceleration is terminated abruptly by high-magnitude lake-drainage that resets the glacier to a ‘quiescent’ state for several years. The 2022 event exemplifies this process: the near-terminus ice velocity accelerated briefly from a pre-event baseline of ~200 m a−1 to ~1000 m a−1 before dropping to ~50 m a−1 over subsequent years. Each GLOF releases an immense meltwater volume (mean discharge in 2022 ~17000 m³ s−1), carving a ~1.5-km-wide, efficient subglacial channel. This channel enables extensive lowering of the subglacial water pressure, increasing ice–bed friction and suppressing ice motion. As climate warming increases GLOF frequency, this powerful negative feedback will modulate ice sheet motion acting as a brake on ice-dynamics at the margins of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

title: Encoding information into an embroidery of topological defects in liquid crystals
abstract: A photopatterned alignment layer with a periodic lattice of vortices acts as a substrate for pinned defect lines in a liquid crystal. These topological defect lines can be rearranged by optical manipulation into a vast number of states that can store information.

title: Diminished subsurface oxygen maximum linked to rapid decline of the North Pacific Central Mode Water
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mode waters strongly shape ocean heat storage and oxygen uptake, yet their persistence under continued warming remains unclear. Here we show a rapid decline in the North Pacific Central Mode Water (CMW) since the early 2020s, leading to a marked reduction in the subsurface oxygen maximum at Station ALOHA, the monitoring site for the Hawaii Ocean Time-series program, 50 km north of Oahu. In general, weakened westerlies over recent decades have intensified surface warming and stratification, suppressing CMW renewal, whereas strong El Niño typically strengthens the westerlies and promotes vigorous CMW formation. In contrast, we find that the strong 2023–2024 El Niño failed to reinvigorate the CMW because the El Niño–related atmospheric teleconnection pattern shifted unusually far east of the formation region. Similar atmospheric anomalies are projected under future warming scenarios, implying inhibited surface-thermocline exchanges due to failed mode water ventilation, with consequences for climate, biogeochemical cycles, and marine ecosystems.

title: Enantioselective Enyne Cyclization to Thermodynamically Favored Endocyclic Alkenes via a Rhodium‐Migration Relay
abstract: ABSTRACT Transition‐metal‐catalyzed addition/cyclizations of electrophile‐tethered alkynes constitute one of the most powerful and broadly applicable strategies for the step‐economical construction of cyclic alkenes. However, these reactions overwhelmingly furnish exocyclic products because the catalytic cycle typically terminates upon kinetically favored ring closure, even though the corresponding endocyclic alkenes are thermodynamically more stable. Herein, we report a catalytic enantioselective arylative cyclization of 1,n‐enynes that directly delivers thermodynamically favored endocyclic alkenes bearing an exocyclic stereogenic carbon center in high yields with excellent chemo‐ and enantioselectivities. Deuterium‐labeling experiments and control studies support a pathway in which the catalytic sequence, rather than terminating after the initial arylative ring closure, continues through a formally circuitous relay of sequential 1,2‐, 1,3‐, and 1,4‐rhodium migrations. This migration relay ultimately transposes the C═C bond to the thermodynamically favored endocyclic position, stereospecifically transfers chirality to the exocyclic stereogenic carbon center, and returns rhodium to its initial carbon attachment site. This work not only establishes a distinct mode of catalytic cyclization but also elucidates the previously unknown mechanism underlying this unusual reactivity.

title: Enantioselective C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Radical Coupling Through Photoinduced Electron Donor–Acceptor Activation
abstract: ABSTRACT The enantioselective construction of C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) bonds via radical pathways remains a formidable challenge, particularly when two transient alkyl radicals must be selectively coupled within a chiral catalytic environment. Here we report a photoinduced enantioselective C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) radical coupling for the synthesis of α‐fluoroalkylated secondary alcohols, enabled by dual electron donor–acceptor (EDA) activation and chiral nickel catalysis. Central to this approach are two EDA activation events: one directly generates a primary alkyl radical from a carboxylic acid‐derived redox ester, whereas the other generates an alkoxy radical that undergoes intramolecular 1,2‐hydrogen atom transfer to form a secondary α‐oxy alkyl radical. Stereocontrolled interception of these radicals by a chiral nickel complex enables enantioselective C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) bond formation. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope and functional‐group tolerance, including the late‐stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies further support the proposed asymmetric radical coupling pathway.

title: Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to skin homeostasis, but the antigenic targets remain unclear. Whilst CD1a is known to present lipid antigens to effector T cells, the possibility of CD1a presentation to Treg cells us not fully understood. Here, we show CD1a reactivity in subsets of human circulating and cutaneous CD4+ Treg cells, displaying αβ T cell receptors (TCRs), memory phenotypes and suppressive functions, including the ability to secrete interleukin-10 (IL-10) in response to the permissive lipid antigen lysophosphatidylcholine, known to be enriched in skin inflammation. Moreover, CD1a-reactive IL-10-producing CD4+ Treg cells from patients with psoriasis up-regulate type 1 and type 17 pro-inflammatory signatures under in vitro stimulation, while a corresponding Treg cell population is enriched and dysfunctional in psoriatic lesions. Spatial transcriptomic analyses suggest that CD1a-reactive Treg cell signatures are localized in close proximity to CD1a⁺ antigen-presenting cells within psoriatic lesions and are potentially connected through ligand-receptor interactions relevant to cell-cell contact, recruitment, and functional regulation. Furthermore, clonally expanded IL-10-producing Treg cells retain their suppressive phenotype in a CD1a-dependent and TCR-dependent manner. Together, these findings show that subsets of Treg cells are directed to self-lipid antigens and CD1a, but show an altered phenotype equipped with pro-inflammatory potential in the setting of psoriasis.

title: A Programmable α‐Aminonitrile Platform for Tunable and Stimulus‐Responsive Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN) Delivery
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite increasing evidence that endogenous cyanide participates in cellular signaling, its biological functions remain poorly understood because programmable chemical control over hydrogen cyanide (HCN) delivery has been unavailable. Here we establish a general chemical framework that enables controlled HCN delivery by exploiting the retro ‐Strecker reactiveity of α‐aminonitriles under physiologically compatible conditions. We uncover a predictable structure–reactivity relationship that allows HCN release kinetics to be rationally programmed over more than three orders of magnitude, with half‐lives ranging from 2.9 to 9165 min, primarily through nitrogen‐centered electronic effects with additional steric and conformational modulation. This unified framework further supports multiple modes of molecular control, enabling esterase‐responsive intracellular HCN delivery, ROS‐responsive activation that protects against ischemia–reperfusion injury in both OGD/R cells and MCAO mice, and bioorthogonally triggered HCN generation that suppresses LPS‐induced TNF‐α production in macrophages. Together, these studies establish α‐aminonitriles as an enabling platform that converts cyanide from an experimentally intractable toxic molecule into a chemically programmable signaling entity, providing a molecular foundation for systematic investigation of cyanide biology and its therapeutic potential.

title: Long‐Lived Fluorinated Foldamer Channels Conduct Protons Through a Plausible Confined Carbonyl–Water Relay
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial proton channels that combine high conductivity with strict exclusion of water and competing ions remain challenging. Herein, we report a series of fluorinated aromatic amide foldamers ( 1 ‐ 6 ) that intramolecularly fold into transmembrane channels with angstrom‐scale pores. The lead compound, channel 1 , features an intrinsic pore diameter of approximately 2.0 Å and mediates rapid H + transport across lipid bilayers, with an EC 50 value of 40 nM (∼6.0 x 10 −7 mol% relative to lipid), a single‐channel conductance of 196.2 pS, and long‐lived open states lasting up to 170 s. Notably, 1 displays high H + selectivity over Cl − , Na +, and K + (selectivity ratios of 192.0, 132.6, and 41.3, respectively) with no measurable enhancement of water permeability. Combined molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, DFT calculations, and hydrogen‐deuterium exchange experiments indicate a predominantly dehydrated pore and support a novel confined hybrid proton‐relay mechanism, in which pyridone carbonyl O‐atoms cooperate with one or a few (protonated) water species, distinct from conventional water‐wire conduction. Beyond its transport function, 1 induces apoptosis and exhibits potent anticancer activity, with IC 50 values of 2.7–5.4 µM against four cancer cell lines.

title: A Novel Metal‐Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework (M‐HOF) Cathode Material for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries (LSBs) are highly promising for next‐generation energy storage devices, yet their practical application is hindered by severe polysulfide shuttling and sluggish sulfur conversion kinetics. Herein, a novel metal‐containing hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF‐21) is constructed and integrated with carbon nanotubes and sulfur as cathode for Li–S batteries. The synergistic combination of hydrogen‐bonding networks and Cu coordination sites enables strong polysulfide anchoring and accelerates sulfur redox conversion. Experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the unique framework structure containing metals and rich abundant hydrogen bonds effectively immobilizes soluble lithium polysulfides, while Cu active centers induce interfacial electronic coupling and optimize the thermodynamic conversion pathway of sulfur species. Benefiting from the adsorption–catalysis synergistic regulation, the HOF‐21/CNT@S cathode exhibits enhanced reaction kinetics, suppressed polysulfide migration, and improved interfacial stability. As a result, the assembled HOF‐21/CNT@S battery delivers excellent long‐term cycling stability with a capacity decay rate of only 0.06% per cycle over 500 cycles at 2 C at room temperature. Moreover, it maintains outstanding low‐temperature adaptability, achieving 76.8% capacity retention after 200 cycles at −10°C and 90.6% retention after 200 cycles at −20°C. This work provides a promising strategy for designing advanced cathode materials toward high‐energy‐density Li–S batteries.

title: Dynamic Oxygen Spillover–Structure Feedback in Asymmetric Site Catalysts: Stability Regimes and Design Principles
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen spillover refers to the transfer of oxygen‐containing species, including adsorbed intermediates and lattice‐derived oxygen, from a donor site/domain to a functionally nonequivalent acceptor through interfacial or connected surface pathways. Despite extensive studies of surface‐confined spillover, its atomic‐scale dynamics in asymmetric multi‐site catalysts remain elusive. This minireview summarizes forward, reverse, and cross‐site oxygen spillover and the key factors regulating these processes. These factors are categorized into intrinsic material properties, including composition, coordination and interfacial structures, and extrinsic operating conditions, such as applied potentials and local electrolyte environments. Moreover, we elaborate on how integrating in situ/operando spectroscopy with theoretical calculations elucidates the structure–activity relationships and dynamic structural evolution at elevated current densities. In particular, drawing on these mechanistic insights, we discuss rational design strategies for asymmetric multi‐atom site catalysts. Specifically, we emphasize how interface engineering, defect control, and self‐optimization methods promote the synergy of spillover effect and structural stability. Finally, we outline the future research direction and emphasize the urgent need to achieve higher space–time resolution in situ characterization and scalable synthesis of uniform asymmetric site catalysts for practical applications.

title: Thermodynamic–Kinetic Synergy Enables Neon/Helium Separation in an Anion‐Pillared Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Separating neon (Ne) from helium (He) remains challenging because both gases are chemically inert and weakly interacting, while classical size‐sieving principles predict faster transport for the smaller He atom. Here we address this challenge with the anion‐pillared metal–organic framework (MOF) Ni(4‐DPDS) 2 CrO 4 , whose confined pores combine narrow apertures with electrostatically heterogeneous cavities. This environment provides multiple weak contacts that favor Ne adsorption while producing an inverse diffusional response relative to the expected size trend. At 77 K and 100 kPa, the framework adsorbs 50.63 cm 3 g −1 of Ne but only 0.40 cm 3 g −1 of He in static adsorption, with a kinetic Ne/He selectivity of 113.58. Fixed‐bed experiments afford He with a purity above 99.999%, followed by temperature‐driven recovery of Ne with a purity above 99.7%. The results show that coordinating adsorption thermodynamics with molecular transport offers a route to separating weakly interacting gases beyond equilibrium affinity or classical size sieving alone.

title: Decoding Direct Regeneration of Spent LiFePO 4 : From Defect Evolution to Thermodynamic–Kinetic Barrier Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid growth of LiFePO 4 (LFP) batteries has made the sustainable recycling of spent cathodes increasingly important for the battery circular economy. Direct regeneration has emerged as the most promising strategy because it preserves the pristine framework, minimizes energy consumption, and maximizes material value. However, the underlying principles governing regeneration remain elusive, as exemplified by the apparent thermodynamic‐kinetic paradox that metallic lithium has been reported to be ineffective for restoring spent LFP, whereas weaker reductants can achieve effective recovery. These observations indicate that regeneration is governed not by thermodynamic driving force alone, but by the coupled effects of electron transfer, ion diffusion, and lattice defects. In this study, we introduce a multiscale defect framework that correlates defect formation energy (Δ H f ), migration barriers ( E a ), and electron‐transfer reorganization energy ( λ ) with different degradation states of spent LFP. A hypothesis that the dominant barrier evolves with degradation was proposed, enabling failure‐dependent strategies ranging from relithiation and phase‐boundary engineering to defect‐guided upcycling. By transforming regeneration from empirical optimization into rational barrier engineering, this perspective provides a unified understanding of diverse restoration pathways. Finally, emerging challenges, including impurity management, AI‐assisted diagnostics, and closed‐loop materials design, are discussed to guide the development of sustainable battery recycling technologies.

title: 3D-MINSTED nanoscopy and protein tracking in densely labelled living cells
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Investigating the movements and conformational changes of proteins in living cells is essential for understanding their function. The recently introduced fluorescence nanoscopy method called MINSTED has successfully tracked single fluorophore-labelled proteins, albeit in fixed cells and two dimensions only.
